executive_summary: A sellable transfusion system must implement the full pretransfusion safety chain, not just an ABO/Rh lookup: a Type & Screen (T&S) sample with a defined validity window, an antibody (alloantibody) screen against a reagent panel, and a documented crossmatch (serologic immediate-spin and/or AHG, or electronic/computer crossmatch when strict criteria are met). It must support emergency uncrossmatched group O release (O-neg RBC, often AB plasma) with retrospective testing and physician sign-off, and encode an MSBOS so requests default to T&S vs crossmatch by procedure to reduce waste. Component production must model a separation/processing event that splits one whole-blood (or apheresis) collection into multiple child products (LR-RBC, FFP, platelets, cryoprecipitate) with full parent→child lineage so any product traces back to the donor and forward to the recipient. Special attributes (irradiated, leukoreduced, CMV-negative, washed, frozen/deglycerolized, antigen-negative) must be first-class, clinically-gated unit properties that the issue logic enforces. ABO/Rh static lookup is unsafe because it ignores clinically significant non-ABO alloantibodies, historical/repeat-sample ABO confirmation, sample validity expiry, antigen-negative requirements, and patient-specific special needs — all of which the crossmatch and antibody records exist to catch.

recommendations.title: Implement Type & Screen with sample validity window and ABO confirmation rule
recommendations.detail: Add a patient_pretransfusion_sample (specimen) entity capturing: ABO group, Rh(D) type, antibody screen result (neg/pos), draw datetime, collector ID, and a computed validity_expiry. Per AABB Standard 5.something / common practice: if the patient has been transfused or pregnant within the preceding 3 months (or history unknown), the crossmatch/compatibility sample is valid only 3 days (sample drawn day = day 0; expires end of day 3). Otherwise institutions may extend. ABO/Rh must be determined on the current sample AND confirmed against a second determination (historical record OR second independently-drawn sample) before non-emergency group-specific issue — this is the AABB requirement to prevent wrong-blood-in-tube (WBIT). System must BLOCK group-specific issue if only a single ABO determination exists with no historical confirmation.

recommendations.title: Model antibody (alloantibody) screen and identification as records, not booleans
recommendations.detail: Add antibody_screen (per specimen: method IAT/PEG/LISS/gel, reagent screen cell lot, result per cell, overall pos/neg, tech ID) and antibody_identification (panel) records. When positive, store identified specificities (e.g., anti-K, anti-E, anti-Fya, anti-Jka) as a structured, persistent patient antibody history (transfusion_antibody_history) that survives across visits and branches — antibodies can evaniesce below detection but still cause hemolysis, so a once-identified antibody must permanently flag the patient and force antigen-negative + AHG crossmatched units thereafter. This persistent record is exactly what a static ABO/Rh table cannot represent.

recommendations.title: Implement crossmatch as a typed, evidenced event with three methods
recommendations.detail: Add crossmatch record linked to (patient_sample_id, blood_unit_id, ordering_request_id) capturing: method = immediate_spin (IS, ABO/major incompatibility detection only), AHG/full antiglobulin (IAT — required when current or historical clinically significant antibody present), or electronic/computer crossmatch; result (compatible/incompatible); tech ID + timestamp; reagent/lot; and unit segment used. ELECTRONIC CROSSMATCH eligibility must be system-enforced and is permitted ONLY when ALL hold: (a) two concordant ABO/Rh determinations on the patient (one current), (b) current antibody screen negative AND no history of clinically significant antibodies, (c) the computer system has been validated to alert on ABO incompatibility, and (d) donor unit ABO/Rh confirmed by the facility. If any condition fails, the system must downgrade to serologic AHG crossmatch. Hard-code these gates; do not allow override without supervisor e-signature.

recommendations.title: Emergency uncrossmatched (massive transfusion) release with retrospective workflow
recommendations.detail: Add an emergency_release pathway: allow issue of group O RBC (O-neg for females of childbearing potential / unknown; O-pos acceptable for males/older to conserve O-neg) and group AB or low-titer A plasma BEFORE crossmatch/screen complete, requiring an ordering physician identity + emergency justification captured at release (cannot be silently bypassed). System must then create mandatory open follow-up tasks: complete ABO/Rh + antibody screen + retrospective crossmatch on the pre-transfusion sample, and a physician sign-off acknowledging uncrossmatched release. Units issued emergency-uncrossmatched must remain flagged in the audit trail. Per AABB the retrospective compatibility testing must still be completed even though transfusion preceded it.

recommendations.title: Encode MSBOS to drive request defaults and the crossmatch:transfusion (C:T) ratio
recommendations.detail: Add msbos table keyed by procedure (and optionally branch) → recommended action: none / T&S only / crossmatch N units. blood_requests should default order type from MSBOS, steering low-bleeding-risk procedures to T&S (no units reserved) rather than holding crossmatched units. Track and report C:T ratio (units crossmatched ÷ units transfused); target ≈ ≤2.0:1. This is both a clinical-safety and inventory-efficiency selling point and directly reduces reservation-lock contention and outdating.

recommendations.title: Model component production as a separation event with parent→child lineage
recommendations.detail: Add component_production (processing) event: input = source collection unit (whole blood or apheresis), output = N child blood_units each with its own ISBT 128 DIN+product code, derived product type, volume, additive solution, and inherited donor/infectious-marker results. One whole-blood unit → typically 1 LR-RBC (in additive solution) + 1 FFP (frozen ≤8h for FFP, ≤24h = FP24) + 1 platelet (from buffy-coat/PRP), and cryoprecipitate is produced by controlled thaw of FFP → 1 cryo + cryo-poor plasma. blood_units needs parent_unit_id (self-referential), production_event_id, and product_code. Lineage must be bidirectional: forward trace (donor→components→recipients, for lookback on a later-positive donor) and backward trace (recipient reaction→unit→donor). This is mandated by EU Directive 2002/98/EC traceability ('vein to vein', 30-year retention) and FDA 21 CFR 606.160.

recommendations.title: Make special attributes first-class, clinically-gated unit properties enforced at issue
recommendations.detail: Add boolean/typed attributes on blood_units: leukoreduced (LR — most cellular products by default; reduces febrile non-hemolytic reactions, HLA alloimmunization, CMV risk), irradiated (gamma/X-ray, prevents transfusion-associated GVHD — required for cellular products to immunocompromised, intrauterine/neonatal exchange, HLA-matched, directed donations from relatives, Hodgkin/hematopoietic transplant patients; irradiation shortens RBC dating to 28 days from irradiation or original expiry, whichever sooner), CMV_negative (donor seronegative — for CMV-safe needs e.g. intrauterine, some neonates, CMV-seronegative pregnant, transplant; LR is often accepted as 'CMV-safe' equivalent), washed (removes plasma — IgA deficiency with anti-IgA, severe allergic/anaphylactic reactions, neonatal where K+ load matters), frozen/deglycerolized (rare/antigen-negative RBC long-term storage; post-deglyc 24h outdate), antigen_negative (specific antigens e.g. K-neg, E-neg, Jka-neg). Add patient_special_requirements per patient; issue engine must MATCH unit attributes to patient requirements and BLOCK issue of a non-conforming unit (e.g., non-irradiated to an irradiation-required patient) with hard stop + override audit.

recommendations.title: Two-person/barcode bedside administration check and transfusion outcome capture
recommendations.detail: Add bedside verification (scan patient wristband DIN + unit DIN, confirm match independently) and transfusion_administration record (start/stop time, vitals, administering staff). Add transfusion_reaction record (type: AHTR/DHTR/FNHTR/allergic/TACO/TRALI/septic, severity, workup) feeding back to the patient antibody/special-requirements history and to hemovigilance reporting. Wrong-blood-in-tube and mis-transfusion are the dominant fatal errors; barcode verification is the single highest-value safety control.

compatibility_rules: keep static ABO/Rh as a FIRST-PASS filter only; demote from sole arbiter — issue gate now requires sample validity + antibody screen + crossmatch/electronic-eligibility + special-requirement match
risks_and_tradeoffs: ABO/Rh static lookup alone misses: clinically significant non-ABO alloantibodies (anti-K, anti-Fya, anti-Jka, anti-E, etc.) that cause acute/delayed hemolytic reactions; antibodies that have evaniesced below current detection but remain in history; required second ABO determination (WBIT detection); sample validity expiry (3-day rule); and patient special requirements (irradiated/CMV-neg/antigen-neg). Issuing on lookup alone is a patient-safety and regulatory failure.

Electronic crossmatch is a software-validated control under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and AABB — selling it means the vendor must provide validation evidence (IQ/OQ/PQ) that the system correctly detects ABO incompatibility and correctly blocks ineligible cases; vanilla PHP/MySQL can implement the logic but the burden is the validation/verification dossier, not the code.

Sample-validity and antibody-history rules are time- and history-dependent; offline-sync branches risk acting on stale antibody history. A patient flagged with anti-K at branch A must not be issued K-untested units at branch B during a sync gap — the offline queue must treat antibody history and special requirements as high-priority/blocking-replication data, or block group-specific issue when history confidence is stale.
Irradiation/deglycerolization change unit expiry dynamically; expiry must be recomputed event-driven, not a fixed field, or expired-product issue becomes possible.

Override pathways (emergency release, electronic-XM downgrade) are necessary but are the most dangerous surfaces; each must carry mandatory identity + reason + e-signature (21 CFR Part 11) and be immutable in audit_logs.

Component lineage demands true bidirectional traceability with 30-year retention (EU Directive 2002/98/EC); MySQL retention/backup and immutable audit are a procurement/compliance obligation beyond schema design.
php_mysql_feasibility: Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX CAN implement the data model and the deterministic gating logic (sample validity, ABO double-determination, antibody-history flagging, electronic-crossmatch eligibility gates, MSBOS defaults, parent→child lineage via self-referential FK, special-attribute matching at issue). None of this requires features the stack lacks. Where the stack is INADEQUATE for the sellable bar: (1) Validation/compliance burden — electronic crossmatch and any computerized compatibility decision are regulated controls under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and AABB; the product needs IQ/OQ/PQ validation evidence, change control, and audit that vanilla code does not provide for free. (2) Immutable, tamper-evident audit — 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures + EU 30-year traceability require append-only/hash-chained audit and controlled record retention; raw MySQL tables are mutable and need application-level enforcement plus DB-level controls (triggers preventing UPDATE/DELETE on audit, periodic integrity hashing). (3) Concurrency at issue — reservation-lock 'intent' is not enough; preventing double-issue of a single unit across branches needs transactional row locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) or optimistic version columns; naive AJAX without DB transactions WILL double-issue under load. (4) Offline-sync of safety-critical history (antibody specificities, special requirements) is a correctness hazard, not a convenience feature; eventual consistency on these fields can kill a patient, so issue must hard-block on stale/low-confidence safety history rather than proceed. (5) Bedside barcode verification needs a hardware/PWA layer beyond plain server-rendered PHP. SUMMARY: feasible to build, but the gap between 'works' and 'sellable to a hospital' is validation, immutable audit, transactional concurrency, and disciplined handling of safety-history under offline sync — these must be engineered explicitly, not assumed.

executive_summary: A sellable region-agnostic blood-bank system must separate UNIVERSAL invariants (full vein-to-vein traceability, irreversible audit trail, segregation/quarantine of untested or non-conforming units, reactive-result lockout, role-based authority checks, electronic-signature accountability, ABO/RhD safety logic) from JURISDICTION-PARAMETERS (deferral periods, donation intervals, age/weight limits, mandatory infectious-disease test panel, record-retention durations, labeling regime, look-back/haemovigilance reporting timelines). The common denominator across WHO Blood Safety guidance, AABB Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion Services, EU Directive 2002/98/EC + 2004/33/EC + 2005/61/EC + 2005/62/EC, and FDA blood-establishment computer software (BECS) expectations is: every donation, component, test result, and disposition must be reconstructable from donor to recipient and back, indefinitely linkable, and protected by validated software. The compliance layer MUST be data-driven: rules, panels, periods, and labels are configuration rows scoped to a deployment/jurisdiction, evaluated by a generic rule engine, NOT hardcoded PHP. 21 CFR Part 11 (closed-system controls 11.10, signature manifestation 11.50, record/signature linking 11.70, signature components 11.100/11.200/11.300) plus the BECS expectation that the vendor's software is validated in the USER's facility (IQ/OQ/PQ + change control) is the hardest bar; vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX CAN meet the functional controls but CANNOT by itself satisfy validation, secure-timestamp, and tamper-evidence guarantees without disciplined added engineering (append-only hash-chained audit, server-authoritative time, locked-down config-change control). Note: live web verification of source text was blocked in this environment (classifier unavailable); citations below are from standards knowledge and should be re-verified against primary text before shipping.

recommendations.title: Build a generic, data-driven compliance rule engine — never hardcode eligibility/deferral logic
recommendations.detail: Donor eligibility, deferral, donation-interval, age/weight, and test-panel rules MUST be stored as evaluable configuration rows, not PHP if/else. Model: a `compliance_ruleset` (versioned, scoped to jurisdiction+deployment+effective-date range) containing `compliance_rule` rows of typed kinds: AGE_MIN/AGE_MAX, WEIGHT_MIN, DONATION_INTERVAL (by component: whole-blood, plateletpheresis, plasmapheresis, double-red), DEFERRAL (temporary with duration, or permanent), HB/HCT_MIN (sex-specific), BP/PULSE ranges, REQUIRED_TEST_PANEL. Each rule carries: operator (>=, <=, between, in-set), threshold value(s), unit, applies-to predicate (sex, component, donor-type), and a human-readable citation field. A single PHP evaluator walks the active ruleset against a donation context and returns pass/defer(until-date)/reject + the triggering rule id. This is the core of region-agnosticism: selling into a new country = loading a new ruleset row-set, zero code change.

recommendations.title: Treat the mandatory infectious-disease test panel as configurable data with mandatory-minimum enforcement
recommendations.detail: Universal minimum panel per WHO and EU 2002/98/EC Annex / 2004/33/EC: HIV (1/2), Hepatitis B (HBsAg), Hepatitis C (anti-HCV), and Syphilis. Jurisdiction add-ons (configurable): HTLV-I/II (EU for first-time donors in some states), HBV/HCV/HIV NAT, anti-HBc, Chagas (T. cruzi, AABB risk-based), malaria, West Nile/Zika (FDA seasonal/risk-based), CMV/sickle for special inventory. Model each as a `test_definition` row with: assay name, target marker, result-interpretation map (reactive/non-reactive/indeterminate→released/quarantined/discarded), repeat-reactive algorithm, and a `mandatory` flag per ruleset. A unit MUST NOT be releasable until every test flagged mandatory-in-this-ruleset has a non-reactive (or jurisdiction-defined acceptable) result. Reactive on any mandatory test = automatic, non-overridable quarantine + donor-deferral + look-back trigger.

recommendations.title: Enforce vein-to-vein traceability as a UNIVERSAL non-configurable invariant
recommendations.detail: EU 2002/98/EC Art. 14 (traceability) + Directive 2005/61/EC require the ability to trace each unit from donor to recipient and vice versa; the system must guarantee 100% traceability. AABB and WHO require the same. Concretely: an immutable chain donor→donation→component(s)→test_results→disposition(issue/transfer/discard)→recipient/patient, each link carrying who/when/device/lot. The ONLY configurable part is the RETENTION DURATION of these records (see retention rule below), not whether the chain exists. Implement as foreign-keyed, append-only event records; never allow a hard delete of any link.

recommendations.title: Make record-retention periods a configurable parameter with a safe global maximum default
recommendations.detail: EU 2002/98/EC Art. 14 / 2005/61/EC require traceability data retained at least 30 years. AABB/US (21 CFR 606.160(d)) requires many records 10 years, some indefinitely. WHO recommends long retention. Model retention as `retention_policy` rows keyed by record-class (donor record, donation, test result, traceability link, audit log, adverse-event report) with a duration per jurisdiction and an enforcement mode (block-purge vs. archive). DEFAULT to the strictest (30y / indefinite for traceability) so an unconfigured deployment is never under-compliant. Retention enforcement must prevent deletion before the period elapses — purge jobs must consult this table.

recommendations.title: Implement 21 CFR Part 11 closed-system controls explicitly (11.10) — this is the validation backbone
recommendations.detail: 11.10(a) system validation (see IQ/OQ/PQ rec); (b) ability to generate accurate, complete human-readable AND electronic copies of records for inspection; (c) protection of records over retention period; (d) limiting system access to authorized individuals; (e) secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails recording operator entries/changes WITHOUT obscuring prior values, retained as long as the record; (f) operational system checks enforcing sequencing of steps/events; (g) authority checks (only authorized users perform signings/actions); (h) device checks where relevant; (i) personnel training/qualification controls; (j) written accountability policies for signature misuse; (k) controls over documentation. Map each (a)-(k) to a concrete subsystem and keep a traceability matrix. The audit trail (e) is the single most load-bearing control and must be append-only + tamper-evident.

recommendations.title: Make the audit trail append-only AND tamper-evident (hash-chained) with server-authoritative time
recommendations.detail: 21 CFR 11.10(e) demands secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails that do NOT obscure previously recorded information and are retained for the record's lifetime. Vanilla MySQL audit_logs are insufficient because a DBA/app can UPDATE/DELETE rows silently. Required: (1) audit rows are INSERT-only; revoke UPDATE/DELETE at the DB-grant level for the application account on the audit table; (2) each row stores prev_hash + row_hash (SHA-256 over canonical content + prev_hash) forming a chain so any back-dating/deletion breaks verification; (3) timestamps come from the DB server (UTC), never the client/AJAX caller, to defeat clock spoofing; (4) periodic chain-verification job. This is added engineering the base stack does not give you for free — call it out in the SOW.

recommendations.title: Implement electronic signatures per 11.50 / 11.70 / 11.100 / 11.200 / 11.300
recommendations.detail: 11.50: each signed record must display the signer's printed name, date/time of signing, and the MEANING of the signature (e.g., reviewed, approved, released, verified) — store these and render them on every report/printout. 11.70: signature is linked to its record so it cannot be cut/copied/transferred to falsify another record (enforce by binding signature to the record's content hash). 11.100: each e-signature is unique to one individual, never reused/reassigned; identity verified before issuance. 11.200: non-biometric signatures use at least two components (user ID + password); first signing in a session requires both components, subsequent continuous-session signings require at least one; signings by others require all components. 11.300: controls over IDs/passwords — uniqueness, periodic checks/revisions/expiry, loss-management/de-authorization procedures, transaction safeguards. Critical release steps (unit release after testing, crossmatch sign-off, issue to patient) MUST capture a meaning-bearing e-signature, not just a session.

recommendations.title: Configurable labeling regime with ISBT 128 as the default standard
recommendations.detail: ISBT 128 (ICCBBA) is the international standard for blood/cell/tissue identification: Donation Identification Number (DIN) with check digit, Product Code, ABO/RhD, expiration date, all in linear+Data Matrix barcodes with defined data structures. EU and AABB both move toward/accept ISBT 128; some legacy US sites use Codabar. Model labeling as a `labeling_profile` per deployment: standard (ISBT128 | CODABAR | custom), barcode symbologies, DIN format, product-code dictionary, required label zones, and whether eye-readable + machine-readable both mandatory. Do NOT hardcode label layout. ISBT 128 DIN generation/parsing (incl. check character) and Product Code mapping should be a dedicated module. Flag: true ISBT 128 conformance requires an ICCBBA facility registration number and licensed databases — vendor cannot self-issue.

recommendations.title: Software validation 'in the user's facility' = vendor-provided IQ/OQ/PQ package + change control, not just internal QA
recommendations.detail: FDA blood-establishment computer software guidance and the General Principles of Software Validation make the USER (hospital/blood establishment) responsible for validating the software in THEIR environment. As a vendor you must ship a validation package enabling that: (1) IQ — Installation Qualification: documented evidence the software is installed correctly (versions, DB schema version, environment, dependencies, config baseline); (2) OQ — Operational Qualification: scripted test cases proving each function works to spec across boundary/limit/negative cases (e.g., expired unit cannot be issued, reactive unit cannot be released, ABO-incompatible issue is blocked); (3) PQ — Performance Qualification: the facility runs its own real workflows/data and confirms fitness for use. PLUS: a versioned Requirements Spec + traceability matrix (requirement→test), a Validation Master Plan, and formal CHANGE CONTROL (every code/config change is risk-assessed, tested, version-bumped, re-validated as needed, and logged). Without this package the product is not sellable to a regulated blood establishment regardless of code quality.

recommendations.title: Version and scope every compliance configuration; never edit config in place
recommendations.detail: Because a unit released yesterday must be judged against the rules in force yesterday, compliance config MUST be temporally versioned. Each ruleset/test-panel/retention/labeling profile carries effective_from/effective_to and is immutable once activated; changes create a NEW version. Disposition records store the ruleset_version_id used so historical decisions are reconstructable and defensible to an auditor. Config changes themselves are signed (11.50) and audit-trailed (11.10e) and run through change control. This closes the loop between Part 11 change control and the data-driven rule engine.

recommendations.title: Designate Responsible Person + role/competency model in data
recommendations.detail: EU 2002/98/EC Art. 9 requires a designated 'responsible person' for each blood establishment; AABB requires a qualified medical/technical director and defined personnel competencies. Model roles, qualifications, training records, and per-action authority as data (authority-check source for 11.10(g)). Certain actions (final unit release, deviation approval, recall authorization) are restricted to roles flagged with the requisite qualification, and the responsible-person identity per branch is a configured, auditable field.

recommendations.title: Configurable haemovigilance / serious adverse event & reaction (SAE/SAR) and look-back reporting
recommendations.detail: EU Directive 2005/61/EC mandates notification of serious adverse events and reactions; AABB and WHO require haemovigilance and look-back. Reporting CONTENT (severity grading, imputability scale, data fields) is largely common, but RECIPIENTS, TIMELINES, and FORMATS are jurisdiction-specific. Model an `adverse_event` subsystem with configurable report templates and submission deadlines per jurisdiction, plus an automatic look-back trigger when a donor later tests reactive (find all prior components/recipients via the traceability chain). Export should target HL7 v2 / FHIR AdverseEvent + BiologicallyDerivedProduct resources for interoperability rather than a proprietary format.

recommendations.title: Use HL7 v2 / FHIR as the interoperability boundary, not a custom API
recommendations.detail: To be sellable into real hospitals the system must exchange with HIS/LIS. Universal expectation: inbound test results (HL7 v2 ORU / FHIR Observation, DiagnosticReport), blood orders (OML/ORM / FHIR ServiceRequest), patient/encounter context (ADT / FHIR Patient, Encounter), and product representation (FHIR BiologicallyDerivedProduct, SupplyDelivery). Treat this mapping as a configurable interface profile per site. Vanilla PHP can produce/parse these but needs a real HL7/FHIR library, not string concatenation; call out the integration-engine gap.

recommendations.title: Classify each compliance parameter explicitly as UNIVERSAL or CONFIGURABLE in the design doc
recommendations.detail: UNIVERSAL (hardcoded invariants, safety-critical): existence of full traceability; quarantine-until-tested; reactive-result lockout from release; ABO/RhD compatibility enforcement on issue; no-issue-past-expiry; append-only audit; authority checks; unique non-reusable signatures; segregation of conforming vs non-conforming inventory. CONFIGURABLE (per-jurisdiction data): deferral periods & reasons, donation intervals per component, donor age/weight/Hb thresholds (sex-specific), mandatory test panel composition, record-retention durations per record-class, labeling standard/format, SAE/SAR report templates & deadlines, look-back depth, units of measure & locale, signature-component policy (password vs biometric), required consents. Shipping this explicit table is itself a compliance deliverable auditors will ask for.

recommendations.title: Provide audit-export and human-readable record reproduction for inspectors (11.10(b))
recommendations.detail: Inspectors must obtain accurate, complete copies in both human-readable and electronic form. Build a one-click, signature-and-meaning-bearing export per donor/donation/unit/recipient producing a PDF (human-readable) + structured file (CSV/JSON/HL7), including the full audit trail for that object and the ruleset version applied. This is a hard Part-11 acceptance gate and is easy to forget until an inspection fails.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Vanilla PHP/MySQL gives no native tamper-evidence: the append-only hash-chained audit trail, DB-level revocation of UPDATE/DELETE on audit/signature tables, and server-authoritative UTC time are ADDED engineering. If skipped, 21 CFR 11.10(e) is not met and the product fails a serious Part-11 audit.

FDA 21 CFR Part 11 / BECS validation is the USER's facility-level obligation — the vendor CANNOT certify the product as '21 CFR Part 11 compliant' in the abstract. The deliverable is a validation PACKAGE (IQ/OQ/PQ, VMP, traceability matrix, change control) enabling the facility to validate. Marketing the software as 'Part 11 certified' is false and a liability.

True ISBT 128 conformance requires ICCBBA registration (facility number, licensed databases for Product Codes), which the end-customer must obtain; the vendor cannot mint conformant DINs/Product Codes unilaterally. Default labeling must therefore be a configurable profile, and ISBT128 conformance is gated on customer registration.

The offline-sync queue conflicts with append-only hash-chaining and server-authoritative time: offline-created records cannot be trusted for timestamps or chain position until reconciled. Reconciliation must re-stamp with server time, re-link the hash chain on sync, and must NEVER allow offline-created release/issue of a unit whose mandatory tests were not server-confirmed — otherwise traceability and reactive-lockout invariants break.

Configurable rule engine adds power but also risk: a misconfigured ruleset could permit an unsafe donation/release. Safety-critical invariants (ABO/RhD compatibility, reactive lockout, expiry, quarantine-until-tested) must be UNIVERSAL hardcoded guards that the config layer cannot override, only tighten.

Retention defaults must fail safe to the strictest (30y / indefinite for traceability per EU 2002/98/EC). An unconfigured or under-configured deployment must never purge below the global maximum, or it silently becomes non-compliant.

Temporal versioning of compliance config increases query/schema complexity (every disposition must record the ruleset_version applied). Omitting it makes historical decisions indefensible to auditors, so the complexity is non-negotiable.

HL7 v2 / FHIR interoperability cannot be done with PHP string concatenation at the sellable bar; a real HL7/FHIR library or integration engine is required, which is outside the assumed stack and must be budgeted.

Multi-branch + region-agnostic means a single deployment may span jurisdictions with conflicting rules (e.g., different deferral periods). The model must bind each BRANCH/establishment to its own jurisdiction+ruleset, not assume one global config per install.

php_mysql_feasibility: Vanilla PHP + MySQL + HTML/JS/AJAX CAN meet the FUNCTIONAL compliance controls (data-driven rule engine, configurable test panels/deferrals/retention/labeling, role-based authority checks, e-signature capture with meaning, traceability chain via foreign keys, HL7/FHIR export). It CANNOT meet the sellable bar out of the box on four fronts, each requiring deliberate added engineering: (1) TAMPER-EVIDENCE / 11.10(e): MySQL rows are mutable; you must make audit and signature tables INSERT-only by revoking UPDATE/DELETE at the DB-grant level for the app account, add a SHA-256 prev_hash→row_hash chain, and add a periodic chain-verification job — none of which the stack provides natively. (2) TRUSTED TIME: AJAX clients cannot be trusted for timestamps; all compliance timestamps must come from the DB server in UTC, and the offline-sync queue must re-stamp/re-link on reconciliation. (3) E-SIGNATURE BINDING / 11.70: signatures must bind to a content hash of the signed record so they cannot be transplanted — requires hashing discipline, not just a 'signed_by' column. (4) VALIDATION / BECS: no amount of PHP makes the product 'Part 11 compliant' by itself; the vendor must ship an IQ/OQ/PQ validation package, requirements-to-test traceability matrix, Validation Master Plan, and formal change-control process so the customer facility can validate in their environment — this is documentation/process engineering outside the code. Additionally, real HL7/FHIR and true ISBT 128 conformance need licensed libraries/registration (ICCBBA) the bare stack lacks. PLAINLY: the stack is adequate for the application logic but inadequate, unaided, for tamper-evidence, trusted time, signature binding, and the validation/change-control regime — these gaps must be explicitly engineered and budgeted, or the system is not sellable to a regulated blood establishment.

executive_summary: A sellable multi-hospital blood bank must abandon generic QR codes and adopt ISBT 128 (ICCBBA ST-001) as its native identification and labeling scheme: a globally unique 13-character Donation Identification Number (DIN), structured Product Description Codes, ABO/Rh and special-attribute data structures, and expiry encoded in the ICCBBA-mandated symbologies (linear Code 128 for the base label, Data Matrix ECC200 for the compact 2D/"Eye-readable + machine" label). The system must register for an ICCBBA Facility Identification Number (FIN) per legal entity and license the ISBT 128 database (Product Description Code tables, country codes, etc.), because the codes are externally governed lookup tables that change — they cannot be hand-coded as a static enum. Interoperability is not optional for sale beyond a single silo: hospitals run a HIS/EHR (patient identity, ADT), a LIS (orders/results), and increasingly an FHIR API gateway, and they will require the blood bank to (a) consume ADT/patient demographics, (b) exchange transfusion/compatibility-test orders and results via HL7 v2 OML/ORM and OUL/ORU (with BTS-specific segments BPO, BTX, TCD, and SAC/specimen), and (c) report the actual transfusion act back to the EHR (FHIR BiologicallyDerivedProduct + MedicationAdministration/Procedure, or HL7 v2 transfusion ORU). Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX can host the data and render ISBT 128 labels, but it cannot by itself meet the integration bar: it needs a real HL7 interface engine (MLLP/TCP listener, message queue, ack handling), a FHIR-conformant REST facade, certified ISBT 128 label rendering, and validated check-character/symbology generation — none of which are AJAX-over-HTTP concerns. Say plainly: a single-silo PHP app with QR codes is unsellable to an accredited hospital; the interoperability and labeling layers are a separate, standards-validated subsystem.

recommendations.title: Adopt ISBT 128 DIN as the primary unit identifier (replace internal/QR IDs)
recommendations.detail: Implement the ISBT 128 Donation Identification Number per ICCBBA Data Structure 001. Structure: 13 visible characters = 5-char alphanumeric Facility Identification Number (FIN, ICCBBA-assigned, first char is a country/registration prefix) + 2-digit year + 6-digit serial number, followed by 2 supplementary 'flag' characters (one of which carries the ISO 7064 MOD 37-2 check character computed over the 13 data chars). The barcode data identifier is '=' . Store DIN as a first-class immutable column; never reuse, never let two facilities collide (uniqueness is guaranteed by the FIN, which is WHY a per-branch/per-legal-entity FIN registration with ICCBBA is mandatory). Each branch that independently collects/labels must have its own FIN.

recommendations.title: Register with ICCBBA and license the ISBT 128 reference tables
recommendations.detail: Obtain a Facility Identification Number (FIN) and an annual ICCBBA registration per facility, and license the ISBT 128 Database (Product Description Code table ~ thousands of entries, Special Testing codes, Country/Collection codes, container manufacturer codes). These are externally maintained and versioned; the app must load them as reference data and support periodic updates — they CANNOT be a static hardcoded list. Build a 'reference data import' job (CSV/Excel from ICCBBA) feeding lookup tables.

recommendations.title: Implement Product Description Codes (Data Structure 003) instead of free-text component names
recommendations.detail: Every component (e.g. RED BLOOD CELLS LEUKOCYTES REDUCED, FRESH FROZEN PLASMA, APHERESIS PLATELETS) must carry an 8-char Product Description Code: 5-char product code + 3 attribute chars (collection type, intended use/division, etc.) per ICCBBA Reference Table. This encodes anticoagulant, additive, leukoreduction, irradiation, CMV-negative, washed, divided/split (E-codes for splits), volume class. Map your internal component catalog onto these codes; the human-readable component name on the label MUST be the ICCBBA-defined text for that code.

recommendations.title: Encode ABO/Rh, expiry, and special attributes in their own ISBT 128 data structures
recommendations.detail: Use Data Structure 002 for ABO/RhD blood groups (with the 'biohazard/blood group confirmation' flagging), Data Structure 005 for Expiration Date (and Data Structure 006 when expiration time is needed for short-dated platelets), Data Structure 004 for Collection Date, and Data Structure 022/023 for Special Testing / red cell antigens (e.g. CMV-neg, sickle-neg, antigen phenotype). Expiry must be machine-readable on the label, not just printed.

recommendations.title: Use ICCBBA-mandated symbologies: Code 128 (linear) + Data Matrix ECC200 (2D); drop QR
recommendations.detail: ISBT 128 label production specifies linear barcodes in Code 128 symbology with defined Data Identifier prefixes ('=' for DIN, '=<' for product code, '=%' for ABO/Rh, '=>' for expiry per the standard's data identifier scheme), arranged in the canonical four-quadrant label layout (DIN top-left, Product top-right, ABO/Rh bottom-left, Expiry bottom-right). The 2D option is Data Matrix ECC200 (NOT QR), which can concatenate multiple data structures into one symbol for handheld scanning. QR is inadequate because: (1) it is not part of the ISBT 128 standard, so scanners/LIS at accredited sites will not parse it; (2) it has no defined data-identifier/concatenation grammar for blood data structures; (3) it provides no standardized check-character validation tied to the DIN; (4) AABB/regulatory and HIS vendors expect Code 128/Data Matrix; a QR label fails interoperability and likely accreditation. Implement a validated label-rendering module producing exact barcode dimensions, quiet zones, and human-readable interpretation lines.

recommendations.title: Stand up a real HL7 v2 interface engine (MLLP listener), not AJAX endpoints
recommendations.detail: Hospitals integrate the blood bank/transfusion service via HL7 v2.x over MLLP (Minimal Lower Layer Protocol) on TCP. You must run a persistent listener that frames messages (VT...FS CR), validates, sends ACK/NAK (MSA), persists, and retries. Support inbound ADT (A01/A04/A08/A40 merge) for patient identity, ORM^O01/OML^O21 for orders (type & screen, crossmatch, issue), and emit ORU^R01/OUL^R22 for results. Blood-bank-specific segments: BPO (Blood Product Order), BTX (Blood Product Transfusion/Disposition), TCD, SAC/SPM (specimen/container), and the dispense in OMB/RDE patterns. PHP CANNOT do this as request/response AJAX; you need a long-running daemon (separate service, e.g. a PHP CLI worker or a dedicated engine like Mirth/NextGen Connect) plus a message queue and dead-letter handling.

recommendations.title: Expose a FHIR R4 REST facade for modern EHR integration
recommendations.detail: Implement FHIR resources: Patient + (often) Coverage for identity; ServiceRequest for the transfusion/compatibility order; Specimen for the sample; Observation for blood-group, antibody-screen, crossmatch results (LOINC-coded); BiologicallyDerivedProduct (R4) / BiologicallyDerivedProduct + BiologicallyDerivedProductDispense (R5) for the unit itself; MedicationAdministration or Procedure for the transfusion event reported to the EHR; DiagnosticReport for the transfusion-service report; Provenance for traceability. Support read + search + (where the EHR pushes) create, with a CapabilityStatement. Use US Core / IPS-style profiles where applicable and LOINC/SNOMED/the ISBT 128 code system (FHIR has a defined ISBT 128 NamingSystem/OIDs) for unit identifiers. A FHIR facade is the increasingly mandatory path for selling beyond legacy v2 sites.

recommendations.title: Define explicit integration points for HIS, LIS, and EHR
recommendations.detail: (1) PULL patient identity from HIS: subscribe to ADT feed (v2) or query FHIR Patient/$match; never let staff retype MRN/name — vein-to-vein traceability requires the authoritative patient ID. (2) ORDER exchange with LIS: receive type&screen/crossmatch/issue orders (OML^O21 / ServiceRequest), return results (OUL^R22 / Observation+DiagnosticReport); reconcile specimen IDs (SPM/Specimen) to enforce the one-sample/electronic-crossmatch rules. (3) REPORT transfusion to EHR: on issue and on confirmed transfusion, emit BTX disposition / MedicationAdministration so the EHR records the act, the DIN, lot/expiry, volume, reactions, and links to the patient record. Each is a named, versioned interface with its own conformance profile and test harness.

recommendations.title: Build positive patient/unit ID at the bedside (barcode verification, vein-to-vein)
recommendations.detail: Scan patient wristband + unit ISBT 128 + crossmatch tag at issue and at administration; the system must verify DIN-to-patient reservation, ABO/Rh compatibility, expiry, and special requirements (irradiated/CMV-neg) electronically before transfusion. This closed-loop step is an AABB/Joint-Commission expectation and a core selling point; it depends entirely on machine-readable ISBT 128, which generic QR cannot satisfy across vendor scanners.

recommendations.title: Map your static compatibility_rules table to standards-coded vocabularies
recommendations.detail: Express compatibility, antigen, and special-attribute logic in terms of ISBT 128 codes and LOINC/SNOMED, not internal strings, so results and rules are portable to LIS/EHR. Keep the rule engine but key it on the coded attributes carried in the Product Description Code and ABO/Rh data structures.

recommendations.title: Treat label generation and interface messages as validated, version-pinned artifacts
recommendations.detail: Under 21 CFR Part 11 / accreditation, label layouts, barcode encodings, and message mappings are validated configuration. Version every Product Description Code table load, every label template, every HL7/FHIR mapping; keep an audit trail of which version produced each label and each message (ties into your audit_logs). Provide test/print-verification mode and a barcode read-back self-test.

recommendations.title: Provide an interface conformance & onboarding toolkit per hospital
recommendations.detail: Ship configurable connection profiles (host/port/MLLP vs FHIR endpoint, message-type filters, segment field maps, character set UTF-8/ISO-8859, ACK mode), plus a simulator and conformance test suite, because every hospital's HIS/LIS dialect differs slightly. Selling to multiple hospitals means each site is an integration project; productize it.

Generic QR codes are a hard blocker for sale: accredited hospitals, their LIS/HIS, and their handheld scanners expect Code 128 / Data Matrix with ISBT 128 data identifiers; shipping QR makes the product non-interoperable and likely fails accreditation. This invalidates the current 'generic QR' assumption in the plan.

HL7 v2 over MLLP requires a persistent TCP daemon, message framing, ACK/NAK, queuing, retry, and character-set handling — architecturally outside vanilla request/response PHP+AJAX. Realistically you bolt on an interface engine (e.g. Mirth/NextGen Connect) or a dedicated long-running worker service; the PHP web app becomes one component, not the integration layer.

FHIR conformance (CapabilityStatement, profiles, terminology binding to LOINC/SNOMED/ISBT 128 NamingSystem) is non-trivial; partial/ad-hoc FHIR will be rejected in EHR vendor certification (e.g. Epic/Cerner connectivity programs).

Every hospital is a bespoke integration (segment/field-level mapping differences, ADT event subsets, MRN namespaces); selling to many sites means productizing an onboarding/conformance toolkit or carrying high per-site integration services cost.

21 CFR Part 11 / EU Blood Directive treat label templates, barcode encoders, and message mappings as validated configuration: changes require versioning, validation evidence, and audit trails, slowing release cadence.

Check-character (ISO 7064 MOD 37-2) and symbology generation must be validated against ICCBBA test vectors; a subtle encoding bug produces unscannable or mis-identified units — a patient-safety and liability risk, not a cosmetic one.
Time-precise expiry for platelets (DS-006) and split/divided products (E-codes) add edge cases the inventory/reservation logic must handle correctly to avoid issuing expired or wrong-fraction units.

php_mysql_feasibility: Mixed. MySQL is fully adequate to MODEL ISBT 128 (DIN, product/ABO/expiry codes, reference tables, version history) and to store HL7/FHIR payloads. PHP can RENDER ISBT 128 labels if you add a validated barcode library producing Code 128 and Data Matrix ECC200 with correct data identifiers, quiet zones, human-readable lines, and ISO 7064 MOD 37-2 check characters — generic QR libraries are NOT acceptable. Where vanilla PHP+AJAX breaks at the sellable bar: (1) HL7 v2 integration requires a persistent MLLP/TCP daemon with framing, ACK/NAK, queuing, retry, and character-set handling — this is not a web request/response concern; you must run a long-lived worker service or, more realistically, a dedicated interface engine (Mirth/NextGen Connect) alongside the PHP app. (2) A FHIR facade demands conformant REST semantics, CapabilityStatement, search params, and terminology binding — implementable in PHP but only as a deliberately built, version-pinned, conformance-tested subsystem, not ad-hoc AJAX JSON. (3) The ISBT 128 code tables are externally licensed/versioned and cannot be a static enum; the app needs an import/versioning pipeline. (4) Validation (21 CFR Part 11) means label encoders and message mappings are controlled, evidence-backed artifacts. Plainly: a single-silo PHP+MySQL+AJAX app with QR codes cannot be sold to an accredited hospital. The path to sellable is to keep PHP/MySQL as the core domain/inventory app but add three standards-validated subsystems — an ISBT 128 label/identity module, an HL7 v2 interface engine (likely external), and a FHIR REST facade — each independently conformance-tested.

executive_summary: A sellable blood bank system must treat the recipient, not just the request, as a first-class persistent entity: a patient registry keyed by a stable patient identifier carrying a longitudinal, immutable blood-group and antibody/alloantibody history that follows the patient across visits and branches, because a historically-identified clinically-significant alloantibody (e.g. anti-K, anti-Jka) must drive antigen-negative selection for life even when the current type-and-screen is negative (AABB Standards; the antibody does not have to be currently demonstrable to be transfusion-relevant). Component lineage must model donation -> processing/manufacturing event -> child component units as a directed acyclic graph so that look-back and recall (ISBT 128 traceability; FDA 21 CFR 606.160/610.46-610.47; EU 2005/61/EC Art. 5-6) can trace every component, intermediate, and pooled product derived from a donation, plus every prior donation by a now-reactive donor, and quarantine them in one operation. Every blood_unit must move through a formal state machine with guarded transitions (you cannot issue a quarantined, expired, reserved-to-another, or failed-QC unit) enforced in the database, not merely in PHP. Audit must be append-only and tamper-evident via per-row hash-chaining plus electronic-signature linkage (21 CFR Part 11 §11.10/§11.50/§11.70, §11.200), so a DBA with table access cannot silently rewrite history without breaking the chain. Vanilla PHP/MySQL can express all of these as schema and triggers, but true tamper-evidence and Part-11 signatures require controls (append-only storage, signing keys, periodic external anchoring) that MySQL alone does not provide and that must be added explicitly.

recommendations.title: Replace free-text patient_name with a persistent patients registry keyed by a stable MPI identifier
recommendations.detail: Create patients(patient_id PK, mpi_uid CHAR(36) UNIQUE /* org-wide master patient index */, given_name, family_name, sex, date_of_birth, national_id_hash, created_by FK users, created_at, merged_into_patient_id NULL FK patients /* for de-dup merges, never hard-delete */, record_status ENUM('active','merged','blocked')). blood_requests.patient_name TEXT is removed and replaced with blood_requests.patient_id FK patients. Identity must be resolvable across branches: add patient_identifiers(id PK, patient_id FK, system VARCHAR /* e.g. 'MRN:BranchA','national-id','passport' */, value, is_primary BOOL, UNIQUE(system,value)) so the same human under different branch MRNs collapses to one patient_id. Map to HL7 FHIR Patient (identifier[], link[] for merges). Rationale: blood-group and antibody history are worthless if they cannot be re-associated to the same person on the next visit; free-text names cause duplicate records and mis-selection.

recommendations.title: Add an immutable, longitudinal patient blood-group history (never a single mutable column)
recommendations.detail: patient_blood_groups(id PK, patient_id FK, abo ENUM('A','B','AB','O'), rh_d ENUM('pos','neg','weak_d','unknown'), method VARCHAR /* gel,tube,analyzer */, determined_at, determined_by FK users, verified_by FK users NULL /* two-person rule for first determination */, branch_id FK, source ENUM('current_testing','historical','external'), sample_id FK samples, is_discrepant BOOL DEFAULT 0, supersedes_id FK self NULL). Append-only: a new typing inserts a row, never UPDATEs. AABB requires a second ABO/Rh determination (or a comparison to a historical record) before issuing non-O/non-D-compatible cellular components; the registry provides exactly this prior record. A trigger raises is_discrepant and blocks electronic crossmatch release when a new typing conflicts with any prior confirmed typing for that patient (ABO discrepancy is a patient-safety stop). Expose latest confirmed ABO/Rh as a VIEW, not a stored column, so history is the source of truth.

recommendations.title: Add a lifelong antibody/alloantibody history that drives antigen-negative unit selection
recommendations.detail: patient_antibodies(id PK, patient_id FK, specificity VARCHAR /* ISBT-aligned: anti-K, anti-Jka, anti-D, anti-E, anti-Fya, anti-c... */, antigen_system VARCHAR /* Kell,Kidd,Duffy,Rh... */, clinical_significance ENUM('significant','insignificant','unknown'), status ENUM('identified','suspected','historical_only','ruled_out'), first_identified_at, first_identified_branch FK, identified_by FK users, last_demonstrated_at NULL, evanescent BOOL DEFAULT 1 /* may become undetectable but stays clinically relevant */, autocontrol_positive BOOL, panel_ref VARCHAR, notes_signed_blob_id FK esign). CRITICAL guard: unit selection for this patient must filter blood_units by antigen-negativity for every specificity where clinical_significance='significant' AND status IN('identified','historical_only'), EVEN IF the current screen is negative — this is the core reason the history must be persistent and cross-visit. Add patient_transfusion_requirements(id PK, patient_id FK, requirement ENUM('antigen_negative','irradiated','cmv_negative','washed','hbs_neg','phenotype_matched'), antigen_spec NULL, reason, active BOOL, set_by FK, set_at) for standing requirements (e.g. irradiated-for-life post-HSCT). Maps to FHIR AllergyIntolerance/Observation + a custom transfusion-requirement profile.

recommendations.title: Model component lineage as donation -> processing_event -> child units (a DAG), supporting splits and pools
recommendations.detail: Keep donations as the apheresis/whole-blood collection. Add manufacturing/processing as first-class events: processing_events(id PK, event_type ENUM('whole_blood_separation','apheresis_collection','split','irradiation','leukoreduction','pooling','wash','aliquot','thaw','pathogen_reduction'), performed_at, performed_by FK, branch_id, sop_version VARCHAR, esign_id FK). Lineage edges: unit_lineage(id PK, processing_event_id FK, parent_unit_id NULL FK blood_units, parent_donation_id NULL FK donations, child_unit_id FK blood_units, relationship ENUM('derived_from','split_from','pooled_into','aliquot_of')). A whole-blood donation produces RBC + plasma + platelet child blood_units via one separation event (parent_donation_id set). A split produces two child units from one parent_unit_id. A pool has multiple parent edges into one child (records donor contributors for pooled-product look-back). blood_units gains: din CHAR(13) /* ISBT 128 Donation Identification Number: 5-char facility + 2-digit year + 6 serial, plus flag/keyboard chars */, isbt_product_code CHAR(8) /* ISBT 128 product description code */, division_id CHAR(2) /* split/aliquot suffix, e.g. A0,B0 */, component_class ENUM('RBC','FFP','PLT','CRYO','WB','GRAN'), parent_donation_id FK donations. Recursive CTE over unit_lineage yields the full ancestor/descendant set for recall.

recommendations.title: Implement a formal blood_unit state machine with DB-enforced guarded transitions
recommendations.detail: States ENUM on blood_units.status: quarantined (default at creation, pre-testing) -> in_testing -> available | failed_qc | discarded. From available: reserved (soft hold for a patient) -> crossmatched -> issued -> transfused | returned_to_stock | wasted. Cross-cutting terminal/exception states: expired, recalled, quarantined_holdback (look-back), transferred_out (inter-branch), destroyed. Define unit_state_transitions(id PK, from_status, to_status, requires_role, guard_rule) as a lookup the application and a BEFORE UPDATE trigger both consult. Hard guards enforced by trigger, NOT just PHP: (a) any -> issued blocked unless status='crossmatched' or electronic-crossmatch-eligible; (b) -> issued blocked if expiry_datetime <= NOW(); (c) quarantined/quarantined_holdback/recalled/failed_qc -> issued is forbidden (no path exists); (d) reserved/crossmatched unit cannot be issued to a different patient_id than the reservation holder; (e) recalled is reachable from ANY non-terminal state and is itself terminal except -> destroyed. Every transition writes a unit_status_events row (append-only: id, unit_id, from_status, to_status, reason, actor FK users, esign_id, occurred_at) — current status is denormalized for query speed but the event log is authoritative. Reject illegal transitions with SIGNAL SQLSTATE in the trigger so a buggy or malicious PHP path still cannot issue an expired/quarantined unit.

recommendations.title: Make audit_logs append-only and tamper-evident via per-row hash chaining
recommendations.detail: Redesign audit_logs(id BIGINT PK AUTO_INCREMENT, seq BIGINT /* monotonic per chain */, occurred_at_utc DATETIME(6), actor_user_id FK, action, entity_table, entity_id, before_json JSON NULL, after_json JSON NULL, branch_id, prev_hash CHAR(64), row_hash CHAR(64), esign_id FK NULL). row_hash = SHA-256(seq || occurred_at_utc || actor || action || entity || before_json || after_json || prev_hash). prev_hash links to the previous row's row_hash, forming a chain: altering or deleting any historical row breaks every subsequent hash and is detectable by a verifier that recomputes the chain. Compute the hash server-side in a single audit-writer code path (or a MySQL BEFORE INSERT trigger) so callers cannot supply their own hash. Revoke UPDATE and DELETE on audit_logs from all application and admin roles; grant INSERT only. Periodically (e.g. hourly) sign the current head row_hash and persist/anchor it externally (separate append-only store, WORM bucket, or notarization) so even root/DBA tampering that recomputes the whole chain is caught by divergence from the anchored head. This is the part vanilla MySQL cannot guarantee alone — see feasibility.

recommendations.title: Add electronic-signature records linked to safety-critical actions (21 CFR Part 11)
recommendations.detail: electronic_signatures(id PK, signer_user_id FK, signed_at_utc DATETIME(6), meaning ENUM('reviewed','approved','released','verified','rejected','quarantine_release') /* 11.50 signature manifestations */, auth_method ENUM('password_reauth','mfa'), reauth_at /* 11.200 requires identity re-verification at signing */, signed_payload_hash CHAR(64) /* binds the signature to exact record content */, audit_log_id FK). Reference esign_id from quarantine release (in_testing->available), QC pass/fail, electronic crossmatch release, issue authorization, recall initiation, and patient blood-group first determination. Part 11 §11.70 requires the signature be cryptographically/linked to its record so it cannot be excised and reused; signed_payload_hash provides that binding. §11.200 requires that a signing not in a continuous session re-authenticate the user — enforce reauth at each signing event. Store the meaning explicitly so the printed/displayed record shows who did what and why (§11.50).

recommendations.title: Add a recall/look-back workflow object that drives mass quarantine and trace queries
recommendations.detail: recalls(id PK, trigger ENUM('donor_seroconversion','positive_repeat_test','recipient_reaction','equipment_failure','recall_notice'), trigger_donor_id NULL FK donors, trigger_donation_id NULL FK donations, marker VARCHAR /* HIV,HBV,HCV,HTLV,syphilis,bacterial */, opened_at, opened_by FK, esign_id, status ENUM('open','tracing','quarantined','dispositioned','closed','reported_to_authority')). recall_items(id PK, recall_id FK, blood_unit_id FK, role ENUM('implicated_component','co_component','recipient_traced'), disposition ENUM('quarantined','destroyed','already_transfused_recipient_notified','not_found'), recipient_patient_id NULL FK patients). On donor seroconversion: recursive CTE over donations->unit_lineage->blood_units for ALL prior donations by trigger_donor_id (look-back window per AABB/regulatory guidance, typically tracing back to a prior negative donation) -> bulk transition reachable in-stock units to quarantined_holdback/recalled, and for already-issued units join issue_transactions to surface recipient_patient_id for clinician notification (EU 2005/61/EC haemovigilance traceability; FDA 610.46-610.47 HCV/HIV look-back). This is the operational reason lineage and the patient registry must both exist and be linked.

recommendations.title: Link issue_transactions to patient_id, the specific crossmatch, and an issue electronic signature
recommendations.detail: issue_transactions gains: patient_id FK patients (replacing any free-text), crossmatch_id FK crossmatches NULL (NULL only when electronic-crossmatch-eligible and recorded as such), issue_esign_id FK electronic_signatures, intended_branch FK, abo_check_passed BOOL. Add crossmatches(id PK, patient_id FK, blood_unit_id FK, method ENUM('serologic_ahg','immediate_spin','electronic'), result ENUM('compatible','incompatible','electronic_release'), antibody_screen_result, performed_at, performed_by FK, verified_by FK). A trigger blocks insert into issue_transactions if the patient has an active antigen-negative/irradiated/CMV requirement not satisfied by the chosen unit, or if abo_check_passed is false — enforcing the patient registry's safety data at the moment of issue.

recommendations.title: Add sample and test-result tables so typings/antibodies are traceable to a specimen and not orphaned
recommendations.detail: samples(id PK, patient_id NULL FK, donor_id NULL FK, collected_at, collected_by FK, sample_type, expiry /* type-and-screen sample validity, e.g. 3 days if transfused/pregnant in prior 3 months per AABB */, accession_number UNIQUE). test_results(id PK, sample_id FK, test_code, result, instrument_id, performed_at, performed_by FK, reviewed_by FK, esign_id NULL). Patient blood-group and antibody history rows reference sample_id, giving each safety-critical fact a verifiable provenance chain (who drew it, when, on what instrument) required for audit and dispute resolution.

recommendations.title: Enforce append-only and transition rules at the database layer, with a hardened DB role model
recommendations.detail: Create a least-privilege MySQL role for the PHP app with INSERT/SELECT/limited-UPDATE but NO DELETE on audit_logs, patient_blood_groups, patient_antibodies, unit_status_events, electronic_signatures, unit_lineage, recall_items. Put the hash-chain computation and state-machine guards in BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers using SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' to reject violations, so enforcement survives application bugs. Provide a separate verifier job (cron) that walks the audit chain and compares the head to the externally anchored head. Document that the DBA/root account is explicitly OUT of the trust boundary for append-only guarantees and is mitigated only by external anchoring — do not claim MySQL triggers alone stop a root user.

DB ROLE change: app role has no DELETE and limited UPDATE on append-only tables; DBA/root explicitly outside trust boundary, mitigated by external hash anchoring.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tamper-evidence vs. DBA power: hash-chaining detects tampering but cannot PREVENT a root/DBA user from rewriting the whole chain. True immutability requires append-only/WORM storage and periodic external anchoring of the chain head (separate system the DBA does not control). MySQL triggers and privilege revocation are bypassable by anyone who can ALTER tables, drop triggers, or use SUPER/root. Do not oversell MySQL-only as tamper-PROOF; it is tamper-EVIDENT only with external anchoring.

Evanescent antibodies: alloantibodies can become undetectable over time yet remain clinically significant. A system that selects units only on the current screen WILL cause a delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction. The persistent patient_antibodies history is the mitigation, but it depends on reliable patient identity matching — a patient-identity false-negative (failed MPI match) silently reintroduces the risk. Identity matching is the single highest-risk dependency.

Patient merges/splits: real MPIs require merging duplicate patients and occasionally un-merging. Merges must carry forward ALL antibody/group history and must themselves be audited and signed; a careless merge can attach the wrong antibody history to a patient (also a safety event). merged_into_patient_id + audit is necessary but merge logic is error-prone.

ISBT 128 licensing/registration: using ISBT 128 DINs/product codes properly requires an ICCBBA facility registration and the controlled product-code/database; a sold system must either integrate the ICCBBA reference tables or support an alternate identifier scheme per region (e.g. Codabar legacy, Eurocode). Hard-coding will not be standards-compliant.

Pooled and irradiated/aliquoted products complicate lineage: a pool has many parents (multi-donor look-back) and aliquots share a parent's test status; the DAG handles this but recall queries must traverse BOTH directions (ancestors for donor-positive look-back, descendants for unit-positive recall) and must include co-components from the same donation.

Performance vs. authority of event logs: making unit_status_events/patient_blood_groups the authoritative source means most queries hit denormalized current-state columns; these must be kept consistent with the event log via the same trigger that writes the event, or drift produces unsafe decisions from stale denormalized state.

21 CFR Part 11 is more than a signature table: it also mandates validation of the system (IQ/OQ/PQ), access controls, operational/device checks, and training records. The data model enables compliance but compliance is a process+validation burden the buyer must complete; the schema alone is not 'Part 11 compliant'.

Append-only growth: hash-chained audit and event tables grow unbounded and cannot be pruned without breaking chains/traceability; need partitioning/archival strategy that preserves chain verifiability across archive boundaries.
php_mysql_feasibility: Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX can fully express the RELATIONAL parts of this lane: the patient registry, longitudinal blood-group and antibody history (append-only via INSERT-only code paths + revoked UPDATE/DELETE), the donation->processing_event->component DAG (lineage edge table + recursive CTEs, available in MySQL 8.0+), the unit state machine (transition lookup + BEFORE UPDATE triggers using SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' to hard-block illegal transitions like quarantined->issued or issuing an expired unit), and the recall/look-back workflow (recursive CTE over lineage + join to issue_transactions for recipient notification). These are correct and implementable on the stated stack and MUST be enforced in DB triggers, not only PHP, so application bugs cannot bypass safety guards. WHERE THE STACK IS INADEQUATE AT THE SELLABLE BAR: (1) True immutability/tamper-PROOF audit is impossible with MySQL alone — hash-chaining makes tampering DETECTABLE, but a DBA/root user can drop triggers, ALTER tables, and recompute the entire chain. Closing this requires controls OUTSIDE MySQL: append-only/WORM storage for the audit stream, periodic signing and external anchoring of the chain head to a system the DBA does not control, and ideally a separate audit microservice with its own credentials. Recommend a dedicated audit-writer service or at minimum a cron verifier + off-box anchored head. (2) 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signatures require cryptographic binding (signed_payload_hash) and re-authentication at signing (§11.200) — implementable in PHP, but key management, MFA, and signing-key custody are NOT a MySQL concern and need a real secrets/KMS solution; storing signing keys in PHP source or the same DB defeats the purpose. (3) MySQL DATETIME has no built-in trusted time; Part 11/haemovigilance need reliable, ideally NTP-synced UTC timestamps and protection against backdating — the app must capture occurred_at_utc server-side and the anchoring process timestamps it externally. (4) ISBT 128 compliance needs the ICCBBA controlled reference tables and facility registration, not just CHAR columns. (5) Concurrency: reservation/crossmatch/issue races on a single unit need SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row locking (InnoDB) to prevent double-issue; AJAX optimistic UIs make this essential and it must be designed in, not assumed. Net: the schema and guards are feasible and should be built DB-enforced; the audit immutability and Part 11 signature/key/time guarantees require components beyond vanilla PHP/MySQL and must be stated to the buyer as such rather than designed around.
