lane: LANE 5 — Concurrency, Reservation Locking & Multi-Branch Offline Sync
executive_summary: A sellable multi-branch blood bank must guarantee that any single blood unit (one physical bag, one ISBT 128 DIN) is allocated/issued exactly once, globally, even under concurrent operators and network partitions. Within a single MySQL instance this is fully solvable with pessimistic row locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) plus a state machine on the unit (available -> reserved -> crossmatched -> issued) and timed reservations with auto-release. Real-time multi-branch visibility via 30s AJAX polling is acceptable for awareness but NOT for correctness; correctness must be enforced server-side at the moment of state transition, never by what the polling UI showed. The genuinely hard, partially-unsolvable part is OFFLINE-then-SYNC: if two branches can independently issue the SAME unit while partitioned, NO merge strategy can un-transfuse blood. Last-write-wins is unsafe because it silently discards one of two conflicting issues. The honest minimum viable architecture is: a single authoritative central MySQL (single source of truth for unit ownership and issuance), branches that degrade to READ-ONLY / queue-only when offline, and exclusive ownership of each physical unit assigned to exactly one branch so a partitioned branch can only commit transitions for units it already exclusively owns. Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX CAN meet the bar ONLY with this architecture and added components (a real-time push channel, an idempotent sync API, and a partition-degradation policy). True multi-master offline-write of shared inventory cannot be made safe and should be refused as a feature.
php_mysql_feasibility:
Single-site concurrency: FULLY FEASIBLE on vanilla PHP/MySQL. InnoDB SELECT ... FOR UPDATE gives exclusive row locks; wrap reserve/issue in START TRANSACTION, lock the unit row, assert state, transition, COMMIT. This is the correct, standard pattern and meets the bar. Confirmed from MySQL docs: FOR UPDATE sets exclusive locks blocking other FOR UPDATE/FOR SHARE/writes until commit/rollback; NOWAIT errors immediately instead of blocking (use for snappy UI), SKIP LOCKED skips locked rows (use for queue-style 'grab next available unit of type X'). Autocommit MUST be off and the whole read-check-write must be inside one transaction — a SELECT then a separate UPDATE without FOR UPDATE is the classic double-allocation bug. Optimistic locking (version column / WHERE status='available') is an adequate, lighter alternative for low contention and is the ONLY option that survives the offline/replay case.

Real-time visibility: PARTIALLY FEASIBLE but with a hard caveat. Vanilla PHP is request/response and cannot push. 30s polling means a unit can appear available in branch B's UI for up to 30s after branch A reserved it. That is acceptable ONLY because the authoritative FOR UPDATE check at commit time rejects the stale action. Polling is fine for dashboards; it is NOT a locking mechanism. True push (WebSockets/SSE) is NOT achievable in vanilla PHP alone — it requires an additional long-running process outside the classic LAMP request model (Ratchet/Swoole/Workerman daemon, or a separate Mercure/Centrifugo/Soketi hub, or Node). That is an added moving part the 'vanilla PHP' framing omits.

Offline-then-sync of SHARED inventory: NOT SAFELY FEASIBLE as multi-master, on ANY stack, not just PHP. This is a CAP-theorem wall, not a PHP limitation. If two partitioned branches can both issue the same unit, the system has lost the single-issuance invariant and no sync algorithm recovers it (you cannot un-issue blood). The PHP/MySQL stack does not make this worse or better — the architecture (who is allowed to write what while offline) is what matters. The stack CAN implement the safe version (exclusive per-unit branch ownership + offline writes restricted to owned units + idempotent central reconciliation).

Verdict: vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX is sufficient for single-site safety and good-enough visibility, but the 'real-time multi-branch + offline-safe shared inventory' promise as literally stated is partly undeliverable and must be re-scoped, plus it silently requires at least one non-vanilla component (a push daemon or hub) to feel real-time.

recommendations.title: Enforce single-issuance with pessimistic row locks inside one transaction
recommendations.detail: Each blood_unit row carries status ENUM('available','reserved','crossmatched','issued','quarantined','discarded','transferred_out'). Reserve/issue path: SET autocommit=0; START TRANSACTION; SELECT status,version,reserved_until FROM blood_units WHERE din=? FOR UPDATE; assert status='available' (or 'reserved' by same request for issue); UPDATE blood_units SET status='reserved', reserved_by=?, reserved_for_request=?, reserved_until=NOW()+INTERVAL 30 MINUTE, version=version+1 WHERE din=?; INSERT audit row; COMMIT. The FOR UPDATE serializes concurrent operators on that exact row so the second loser sees 'reserved' and is rejected. This is the core correctness guarantee and is non-negotiable.

recommendations.title: Use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for 'allocate any compatible unit', NOWAIT for targeted actions
recommendations.detail: When the operator requests a blood TYPE (not a specific bag), select the best candidate with: SELECT din FROM blood_units WHERE abo_rh=? AND status='available' AND expiry>NOW() ORDER BY expiry ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; this lets concurrent operators each grab a different unit without blocking, eliminating contention storms (FEFO allocation = First Expiry First Out). For actions on a specific DIN the operator already named, use FOR UPDATE NOWAIT so the UI fails fast ('unit is being actioned by another user') instead of hanging. Source: MySQL 8.0 InnoDB locking-reads docs confirm SKIP LOCKED removes locked rows from the result and NOWAIT errors immediately.

recommendations.title: Pin isolation level to READ COMMITTED for the OLTP path
recommendations.detail: Default REPEATABLE READ adds gap/next-key locks that increase deadlock frequency on range scans of inventory and can lock phantom ranges you do not intend. Set transaction isolation level READ COMMITTED for the reservation/issue connections to reduce gap locking while still being fully safe because correctness comes from the explicit FOR UPDATE row lock, not from snapshot isolation. Keep statement-based replication OFF (use ROW or MIXED) since NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED are unsafe for statement-based replication.

recommendations.title: Reservation TIMEOUT with auto-release, enforced lazily not by a cron alone
recommendations.detail: Store reserved_until timestamp. Do NOT rely solely on a cleanup cron (cron lag = locked-forever units). Instead make every allocation query treat 'reserved AND reserved_until<NOW()' as available: WHERE status='available' OR (status='reserved' AND reserved_until<NOW()). When a request grabs such an expired reservation under FOR UPDATE, it overwrites it and writes an audit 'reservation_expired_reclaimed' row. Add a low-frequency cron as belt-and-suspenders to flip stale rows back and emit alerts. Typical timeout: crossmatch/hold window per AABB workflow (e.g. 30–60 min reserve, longer explicit crossmatch hold). Make the timeout configurable per hospital.

recommendations.title: Always add a deadlock-retry wrapper
recommendations.detail: InnoDB WILL pick a deadlock victim (ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK 1213) or hit lock-wait timeout (1205) under concurrency. Wrap the transactional function in a retry loop (e.g. up to 3 attempts with small jitter backoff) that re-runs the whole transaction on 1213/1205. Without this, legitimate concurrent issues randomly fail. This is mandatory, not optional, for any FOR UPDATE design.

recommendations.title: Treat AJAX polling as awareness only; enforce at commit
recommendations.detail: 30s polling of an inventory/dashboard endpoint is fine for showing branch stock levels and incoming alerts. NEVER let the client's last-seen state authorize an action. The server re-validates under FOR UPDATE at the instant of the transition. Add an ETag/last_modified or a monotonically increasing inventory_version per branch so polling can return 304/'no change' cheaply and reduce DB load. Poll the change-feed, not the whole table.

recommendations.title: Add a real-time push channel as a separate component, and be explicit it is not 'vanilla PHP'
recommendations.detail: For genuine real-time multi-branch visibility, use Server-Sent Events via a dedicated hub: Mercure (Go binary, SSE, JWT-authorized topics — PHP just POSTs updates to the hub), or Centrifugo/Soketi for WebSockets, or a PHP daemon (Swoole/OpenSwoole, Workerman, Ratchet). SSE/Mercure is the lowest-friction choice: one-way server->client is exactly the visibility need, survives proxies better than raw WS, and PHP stays request/response by publishing to the hub after each committed transaction. Document clearly to the buyer that this is an added always-on process with its own deploy/monitoring — the classic LAMP box cannot push by itself. Keep 30s polling as the fallback when the hub is unreachable.

recommendations.title: Single authoritative central DB for unit ownership; branches are not co-equal masters
recommendations.detail: Designate one central MySQL as the single source of truth for which branch OWNS each physical unit and for issuance facts. Branches read/write against it when online. This collapses the hard distributed problem into the solved single-instance FOR UPDATE problem for the 99% online case. Use MySQL replication (or Group Replication/InnoDB Cluster) for HA of the central node, NOT for multi-master writes of inventory. Multi-primary write topologies (Galera/Group Replication multi-primary) still conflict-resolve at COMMIT and will roll back one of two concurrent issues with a certification error — they do not give you offline writes and add operational complexity; avoid for this domain.

recommendations.title: Offline mode = exclusive per-unit ownership + restricted writes, never shared-inventory multi-master
recommendations.detail: The ONLY safe offline-write model: each physical unit is exclusively owned by exactly one branch at a time (ownership transfer is itself an online, locked, central transaction). A partitioned branch may ONLY reserve/issue units it ALREADY exclusively owns; it may NOT touch units owned by other branches, and inter-branch transfer is impossible while offline (it requires the central authority to move ownership). This makes offline issuance conflict-free by construction: two branches can never issue the same unit because only one owns it. Everything the offline branch does is queued and replayed; because it only acted on units it solely owned, replay never conflicts on issuance.

recommendations.title: Idempotent, append-only event-log sync API; reject last-write-wins for unit state
recommendations.detail: Each offline action is recorded as an immutable event with a client-generated UUID (idempotency key), branch_id, unit DIN, prior_version, action, actor, device timestamp AND server-received timestamp. Sync replays events to the central authority which applies them under FOR UPDATE and is idempotent on the UUID (duplicate replay = no-op). LWW is explicitly banned for unit lifecycle because two 'issued' events for the same DIN are a real-world safety incident (two patients, one bag) that LWW would hide by keeping one and dropping the other silently. Instead: detect the conflict (central already has the unit issued/owned elsewhere), DO NOT auto-merge, raise a CRITICAL reconciliation alert, quarantine the unit record, and force human investigation/look-back per AABB. Non-safety-critical fields (e.g. donor phone edits) MAY use LWW or field-level merge.

recommendations.title: Explain why CRDTs do not save you here
recommendations.detail: CRDTs (e.g. OR-Sets, counters) give conflict-FREE merge but only for data types whose conflicts are semantically mergeable. 'This physical bag was transfused into exactly one patient' is a UNIQUENESS/exclusive-allocation constraint, which is provably NOT expressible as a CRDT under partition (it is equivalent to distributed mutual exclusion, which CAP forbids under AP). A CRDT would happily merge two issuances into a set of two — arithmetically clean, clinically catastrophic. CRDTs are useful for soft state (presence, last-known stock COUNTS for display, comment threads) but cannot enforce single-issuance. Use them, if at all, only for advisory visibility, never for the issuance invariant.

recommendations.title: Partition-issue containment and look-back procedure
recommendations.detail: Accept that the residual risk (a unit issued in two branches) is eliminated by exclusive ownership BUT add defense in depth: (a) at the bedside/issue step require scanning the ISBT 128 DIN + patient ID (electronic crossmatch / positive patient ID) so a double-issue would require the same physical bag in two places, which is physically impossible if ownership is exclusive; (b) on every reconnect, run a reconciliation that flags any DIN with conflicting terminal states and triggers a 21 CFR 11 audit-logged investigation and, if a unit was wrongly distributed, a recall/look-back. Build the alerting and quarantine workflow now, not later.

recommendations.title: 21 CFR Part 11 compliant audit and tamper-evidence on the sync log
recommendations.detail: Every state transition and every replayed offline event must produce an immutable, attributable, time-stamped audit record (who/what/when/old->new) — both branch-local device time and authoritative server time, since offline device clocks drift and cannot be trusted for ordering. Use server-received ordering (Lamport-style sequence or central auto-increment) as the canonical order. Make audit rows append-only (no UPDATE/DELETE; consider hash-chaining each row to the previous for tamper-evidence) to satisfy Part 11 electronic-record integrity and AABB traceability.

recommendations.title: Be honest in the sales/architecture doc about what 'offline' means
recommendations.detail: Sell 'offline-RESILIENT issuance of locally-owned stock with automatic reconciliation', NOT 'full offline multi-branch operation'. Explicitly state: while a branch is partitioned it cannot see other branches' live stock, cannot pull/transfer units from other branches, and can only issue units it already holds. This is the truthful, safe envelope. Promising more is selling a data-integrity failure to a hospital.

risks_and_tradeoffs: CAP wall: single-issuance is a strong-consistency (CP) invariant; you cannot have it AND full offline availability (AP) of shared inventory under partition. Any design claiming both is wrong. The mitigation (exclusive per-unit ownership) buys safe offline at the cost of forbidding cross-branch operations while partitioned — a real functional limitation that must be disclosed.

Pessimistic FOR UPDATE under high concurrency risks deadlocks and lock-wait timeouts; mandatory retry logic adds complexity and, if mis-tuned, tail latency. SKIP LOCKED reduces this but returns an inconsistent snapshot so it must only be used for 'pick-any-available' allocation, never for reporting/counts.

Real-time push requires an always-on non-PHP process (Mercure hub / Swoole / Centrifugo). This breaks the 'vanilla PHP, drop on any LAMP host' selling point and adds deploy, monitoring, and failure-mode surface. If omitted, 'real-time' is really 'up to 30s stale', which must be stated honestly.

30s polling at scale (many branches/users) creates steady DB load; without a change-feed/version/ETag mechanism it does full-table reads repeatedly. Needs the inventory_version + since-seq feed to stay cheap.

Offline device clocks cannot be trusted for ordering; relying on device timestamps for conflict resolution is a latent bug. Must use central server-received ordering as canonical, which means offline actions are only truly ordered upon reconnect.

Reservation timeout tuning is clinically sensitive: too short auto-releases units mid-crossmatch (clinical disruption); too long strands inventory during shortages. Must be configurable and audited, and the lazy-reclaim-on-read pattern must be correct or units leak.

Multi-primary MySQL (Galera/Group Replication multi-primary) looks like it gives multi-branch writes but resolves conflicts by rolling back one committer at COMMIT — it provides neither offline operation nor a free pass on the invariant, and adds heavy ops burden; choosing it under the illusion of 'multi-master = offline-safe' is a trap.

Residual human/process risk: even with exclusive ownership, a manual override or mis-scanned DIN can cause a double-issue. ISBT 128 barcode scanning + positive patient ID at issue is required as the physical backstop; software locks alone are insufficient for the clinical safety bar.

LWW anywhere near unit lifecycle is a silent data-loss/safety failure; if any developer applies a generic 'newest record wins' merge during sync, the system can hide a two-patient-one-unit event. This must be architecturally forbidden and code-reviewed, not left to convention.

executive_summary: A sellable blood-bank system must treat cold chain and hemovigilance as continuous, auditable processes — not static fields. Cold chain requires per-component storage rules (RBC 1–6 °C; platelets 20–24 °C with continuous agitation; FFP/cryo frozen ≤ −18 °C, ideally ≤ −25 °C; thawed FFP 1–6 °C with a short shelf life; whole blood 1–6 °C or 20–24 °C if platelets are to be recovered), continuous time-series temperature logging per storage device and per transport leg, the AABB '30-minute rule' (legacy) / modern validated-time-and-temperature rule for returning issued RBC units to inventory, and automated excursion detection that quarantines affected units pending medical-director disposition. Hemovigilance requires structured capture, ISBT/IHN-conformant classification, severity grading (0–4/death), and imputability grading (definite/probable/possible/unlikely/excluded/not-assessable) for both recipient transfusion reactions (acute & delayed: AHTR, DHTR, FNHTR, allergic/anaphylactic, TACO, TRALI, TAD, TA-GVHD, PTP, TTI/sepsis, hypotensive) and donor adverse events (VVR/syncope, hematoma, nerve/arterial injury, citrate reaction in apheresis), with regulatory reporting timelines (e.g., EU SARE/SAE; FDA fatality notification within prescribed timeframes). Disposal needs a controlled reason taxonomy plus a biohazard chain-of-custody record so wastage reporting is real. Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX can model and report all of this, but CANNOT by itself perform real-time sensor ingestion, alarm-on-disconnect, or guaranteed alarm delivery — those require external IoT sensors/dataloggers, a background worker, and an out-of-band notification path, all of which break the LAMP happy path and must be engineered explicitly.

recommendations.title: Per-component storage rule master table (replace static temperature_range)
recommendations.detail: Create component_storage_spec keyed by component_class with canonical AABB/EU values: RBC/whole_blood store 1–6 °C, transport 1–10 °C, shelf life by additive (CPDA-1 35 d, AS-1/AS-3/AS-5 42 d); platelets 20–24 °C WITH continuous gentle agitation, max 5 d (7 d with approved pathogen-reduction/testing), agitation-interruption tolerance limited (cumulative ≤24 h, single ≤30 min per common SOPs — make configurable); FFP/PF24/cryo frozen at ≤ −18 °C (preferably ≤ −25 °C for 36 mo vs 3 mo), thawed FFP 1–6 °C use within 24 h, thawed cryo 20–24 °C use within 4–6 h; granulocytes 20–24 °C transfuse ASAP (<24 h). Columns: target_min_c, target_max_c, transport_min_c, transport_max_c, requires_agitation(bool), agitation_max_interruption_min, frozen_threshold_c, shelf_life_hours, max_temp_excursion_min, source_standard. Drive ALL alarm logic and the 30-minute/return rule from this table, never hardcode.

recommendations.title: Continuous temperature time-series logging model
recommendations.detail: Add storage_equipment (id, branch_id, type[fridge|platelet_incubator_agitator|freezer|ULT_freezer|transport_cooler|validated_shipper], component_class_allowed, target spec FK, sensor_id, calibration_due, status). Add temperature_log (id, equipment_id, sensor_id, recorded_at[UTC], temp_c, humidity, agitation_ok(bool, for platelets), source[sensor|manual], reading_uuid, ingest_received_at). Index (equipment_id, recorded_at). Expect a reading every 1–5 min per device; this is high-volume — partition by month or roll up to temperature_log_archive. Each manual reading must be operator-attributed for 21 CFR Part 11. Provide AJAX endpoints for sensor POST (token-authed) and for dashboards to poll latest + min/max per window. Also log agitator on/off and door-open events where the device exposes them.

recommendations.title: Excursion detection, quarantine, and disposition workflow
recommendations.detail: Add temperature_excursion (id, equipment_id, component_class, started_at, ended_at, min_temp_c, max_temp_c, duration_min, threshold_breached[low|high|frozen|agitation_stopped], detected_by[auto|manual], severity, status[open|under_review|resolved], disposition[return_to_use|quarantine|discard], reviewed_by, reviewed_at, justification). On breach beyond spec tolerance, auto-create excursion AND auto-set all affected blood_units.status='QUARANTINED' (new status distinct from available/reserved/issued), linked via excursion_unit_link. Units cannot be issued while quarantined. Only blood-bank medical director / qualified reviewer role may release (return_to_use) or discard, with mandatory justification — enforced by RBAC and written to audit_logs. Affected-unit determination = all units in that equipment during the excursion window.

recommendations.title: Equipment alarm + sensor-health model with out-of-band delivery
recommendations.detail: Add equipment_alarm (id, equipment_id, alarm_type[high_temp|low_temp|agitation_failure|power_loss|door_open|sensor_disconnect|calibration_overdue|battery_low], triggered_at, cleared_at, ack_by, ack_at, escalation_level, notes). CRITICAL GAP: a request-driven PHP app cannot detect a sensor that STOPS reporting (the dangerous failure mode) nor deliver alarms when no one is logged in. Require (a) a cron/daemon worker that flags equipment with no reading in N minutes as sensor_disconnect, (b) escalation tiers with timeouts, (c) out-of-band notification (SMS/email/voice via gateway) independent of the browser. State plainly that alarm reliability is a regulated safety function and the LAMP stack alone is insufficient without this background + notification infrastructure and ideally hardware datalogger alarms as the primary safety layer.

recommendations.title: Issued-unit return rule (30-minute / validated time-temperature)
recommendations.detail: Model unit issue/return as events with timestamps. On return of an RBC unit, evaluate against component_storage_spec: legacy '30-minute rule' = if time out of controlled storage >30 min, do not return to inventory; modern AABB approach permits a validated time-and-temperature limit (e.g., surface temp ≤10 °C). Add unit_return_check (unit_id, issued_at, returned_at, minutes_out, measured_return_temp_c, rule_applied, decision[return_to_inventory|quarantine|discard], decided_by). Make the rule (minutes vs measured-temp) configurable per branch SOP. Platelets/thawed products generally not returnable — encode per component.

recommendations.title: Hemovigilance — recipient transfusion-reaction model
recommendations.detail: Add transfusion_reaction (id, patient_id, unit_id(s) via reaction_unit_link, reported_by, onset_datetime, transfusion_start/stop, reaction_category, time_class[acute<24h|delayed], signs_symptoms(JSON checklist: fever, chills, dyspnea, hypotension, hypertension, urticaria, hemoglobinuria, etc.), vitals_pre/post, severity_grade[0..4|death], imputability[definite|probable|possible|unlikely|excluded|not_assessable], investigation_findings, clerical_check_result, lab_results(DAT, repeat crossmatch, cultures, NT-proBNP, etc.), outcome, reportable_to_authority(bool), report_ref, status). reaction_category enumerates ISBT/IHN types: AHTR, DHTR/DSTR, FNHTR, allergic, anaphylactic, TACO, TRALI, TAD, hypotensive, TA-GVHD, PTP, TT-sepsis/bacterial, TTI(viral/parasitic), hemosiderosis, other/unknown. Distinguish TACO vs TRALI explicitly (different timing, BNP, fluid balance, oxygenation criteria). Auto-quarantine co-component units from the same donation pending investigation. Enforce regulatory reporting flags/timelines (EU SARE; FDA fatality reporting; national hemovigilance).

recommendations.title: Hemovigilance — donor adverse-event model
recommendations.detail: Add donor_adverse_event (id, donor_id, donation_id, event_type[VVR/syncope, prolonged_recovery, hematoma, arterial_puncture, nerve_injury/irritation, delayed_syncope_with_injury, citrate_reaction(apheresis), hemolysis(apheresis), air_embolism, allergic, generalized, local_other], onset[immediate|delayed], severity[mild|moderate|severe], with_loss_of_consciousness(bool), with_injury(bool), intervention, outcome, off_site(bool), recovery, follow_up, reported_by, reportable(bool)). Align grading to AABB/IHN-ISBT Donor Standardized Surveillance definitions. Feed donor deferral logic (e.g., severe VVR may alter future donation guidance) and branch QA dashboards. Capture denominators (donations by type) so rates per 1000/10000 donations can be reported.

recommendations.title: Severity + imputability as shared graded vocabularies
recommendations.detail: Implement reusable lookup tables hv_severity_grade (0 no sign/none, 1 minor, 2 moderate/hospitalization, 3 severe/life-threatening, 4 death) and hv_imputability (definite/certain, probable, possible, unlikely, excluded, not assessable) referenced by both recipient and donor events, matching EU Directive 2005/61/EC Annex and ISBT/IHN guidance. Reports (rate, severity distribution, imputability distribution per category) depend on these being controlled vocabularies, not free text.

recommendations.title: Discard/disposal reason taxonomy + biohazard chain-of-custody
recommendations.detail: Add discard_reason lookup with coded taxonomy: EXPIRED, EXCURSION_OUT_OF_RANGE, FAILED_VISUAL_INSPECTION(clots/hemolysis/lipemia/discoloration/leak), POSITIVE_INFECTIOUS_MARKER(HIV/HBV/HCV/syphilis/etc.), QUARANTINE_NOT_RELEASED, BROKEN_COLD_CHAIN_IN_TRANSPORT, RETURN_RULE_FAILED(>30min), CONTAMINATION/POSITIVE_CULTURE, LABEL/CLERICAL_ERROR, LEAKAGE/INTEGRITY_BREACH, QNS/LOW_VOLUME, DONOR_POST_DONATION_INFO, RECALL/LOOKBACK, EQUIPMENT_FAILURE, OTHER(free text required). Add unit_disposal (id, unit_id, disposal_reason_code, decided_by, authorized_by, disposal_datetime, method[autoclave|incineration|licensed_biohazard_contractor], biohazard_batch_id, manifest_ref, witnessed_by, weight_kg). Add biohazard_disposal_batch (id, branch_id, created_at, contractor, manifest_number, sealed_by, collected_at, certificate_ref). This makes the wastage report quantitative (discards by reason, by component, by branch, expiry rate, excursion-loss rate) and satisfies regulated waste tracking.

recommendations.title: Transport/shipment cold-chain capture
recommendations.detail: For inter-branch transfer and hospital dispatch, add shipment_cold_chain (shipment_id, container_id, validated_shipper(bool), packout_config, departure_temp_c, departure_time, arrival_temp_c, arrival_time, embedded_logger_id, logger_data_ref, excursion_detected(bool)). Validated shippers/temperature-monitored transport are expected by buyers; on arrival, an excursion forces receiving-branch quarantine before the units re-enter available inventory.

recommendations.title: 21 CFR Part 11 controls over all hemovigilance/cold-chain records
recommendations.detail: Every disposition (release from quarantine, discard authorization, reaction classification, return-to-inventory) must be an attributed, timestamped, reason-bearing audit_logs entry; records should be append-only with electronic signatures (signed_by, signature_meaning, signed_at) and tamper-evidence (row hashing). MySQL alone does not give you immutability — add application-enforced no-update/no-delete on these tables plus periodic hash-chaining, and say plainly that true WORM/Part-11 compliance needs configuration discipline (DB privileges, signed audit trail) beyond default LAMP.

recommendations.title: HL7/FHIR alignment for interoperability
recommendations.detail: Map reactions to FHIR AdverseEvent + (where applicable) the blood/transfusion context, units to BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and patient/order to ServiceRequest/Encounter; expose temperature observations as FHIR Observation. Even if MVP uses internal tables, design column semantics to map cleanly so a hospital's LIS/EHR integration (a common procurement requirement) is feasible later via HL7 v2 OUL/ORU or FHIR APIs.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Request-driven PHP cannot detect a sensor that stops reporting or deliver alarms when no browser session is open — the most dangerous cold-chain failures (power loss, sensor disconnect) require a background daemon/cron + out-of-band SMS/voice notification; the LAMP stack alone is NOT a compliant alarm system. Hardware dataloggers with independent alarms should remain the primary safety layer.

Temperature logging is high write-volume (per-device readings every 1–5 min × many devices × multi-branch) — MySQL will need partitioning, rollups, and retention policy; naive single-table inserts will degrade. Time-series workloads are not LAMP's strength.
Real-time dashboards via AJAX polling add load and still lag true real-time; WebSockets/SSE are not native to vanilla PHP and need extra infrastructure.

21 CFR Part 11 immutability/electronic-signature requirements are not met by default MySQL — needs enforced append-only privileges, hash-chaining, and signed audit trail; buyers in regulated markets will audit this.

Standards values (platelet 7-day, return-rule specifics, agitation interruption limits) vary by edition/jurisdiction and approved devices — must be configurable per branch SOP, not hardcoded, or the product will be non-compliant somewhere.

TACO vs TRALI differentiation requires clinical data (BNP, fluid balance, oxygenation, imaging) the system may not natively capture — needs structured clinical fields and clinician input, raising data-entry burden.
Offline-sync queue + cold-chain alarms conflict: a branch offline cannot raise/deliver real-time excursion alarms; safety-critical alarming must not depend on central sync.
Sensor vendor heterogeneity (Modbus/MQTT/REST/CSV dataloggers) means the ingest endpoint needs adapters; assuming one protocol will break field deployments.
php_mysql_feasibility: Modeling, classification, disposition workflows, disposal taxonomy, and all hemovigilance/wastage REPORTING are fully feasible in vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX and this is where the stack is adequate. Where it BREAKS for the sellable bar: (1) Continuous sensor ingestion and especially detection of sensor/power LOSS — a request-driven app sees nothing when nothing is sent; you must add a background worker (cron/daemon/queue consumer) outside PHP's request lifecycle. (2) Guaranteed alarm delivery — alarms must reach staff when no one is logged in, requiring an out-of-band SMS/email/voice gateway and escalation engine; browser-based alerts are insufficient and arguably unsafe as the sole mechanism. (3) Real-time monitoring — vanilla PHP has no native push; AJAX polling is a workaround with lag and load cost. (4) High-volume time-series storage — needs partitioning/archival strategy MySQL can do but not by default. (5) 21 CFR Part 11 immutability and electronic signatures — require enforced append-only DB privileges, hash-chaining, and signature semantics layered on top; not provided by default LAMP. (6) Calibrated, validated hardware dataloggers with independent alarms should remain the PRIMARY safety layer regardless of software — the software is the record/QA/reporting system, not the safety instrument. Plainly: build the data model and workflows in PHP/MySQL, but you MUST add a background worker, an out-of-band notification path, and lean on validated sensor hardware; selling this as a compliant cold-chain monitor without those is not honest.

executive_summary: A sellable blood-bank analytics lane must do two distinct things that the plan currently conflates. (1) FORECASTING: predict short-horizon (7–28 day) demand per blood-group×component to drive reorder/collection targets and reservation buffers. For blood banks the practical, defensible methods are moving average, simple exponential smoothing (SES), and Holt-Winters (triple exponential smoothing) for weekly seasonality; heavier ML (ARIMA, gradient boosting, LSTM) is rarely justified at a single hospital's data volume and adds validation, explainability, and 21 CFR Part 11 burden without clear ROI. (2) ANALYTICS/KPIs: compute operational quality indicators a hospital buyer evaluates during procurement — stock-out rate, wastage/expiry rate, crossmatch-to-transfusion (C:T) ratio, days-of-supply, turnaround time, donor return rate, near-expiry inventory. The hard requirement underneath both is a clean, timestamped event log: every state transition of a unit (collected, tested, available, reserved, crossmatched, issued, transfused, returned, discarded, expired, transferred) and every request must be recorded with timestamps, actor, and reason codes. Without that event spine, KPIs are unreliable and forecasting has nothing to learn from. Vanilla PHP/MySQL is fully adequate for KPI computation and for the lightweight forecasting models if run as scheduled jobs (cron) rather than per-request; the gap is that PHP has no native time-series/statistics library, so Holt-Winters and confidence intervals must be hand-coded and unit-tested, and a true scheduler (not request-triggered cron emulation) is required for reproducible nightly aggregation.

recommendations.title: Forecast at the granularity that drives action: group × component × site, daily, short horizon
recommendations.detail: Forecast demand (issues/transfusions) separately per ABO/Rh group (8 groups) × component (RBC, platelets/PLT, FFP, cryo) × branch, on a daily bucket with a rolling 7–28 day horizon. Do NOT forecast total blood demand — it is useless for ordering because O-neg and platelets are the binding constraints. Platelets need their own short horizon (5–7 day shelf life) vs RBC (35–42 day). Output per series: point forecast, and an upper safety quantile (e.g., 90th–95th percentile of demand) used to set the reorder/collection target, because the cost of stock-out (cancelled surgery, emergency O-neg release) is asymmetrically higher than the cost of mild over-collection.

recommendations.title: Method ladder by data availability — degrade gracefully, never error on sparse data
recommendations.detail: Implement three tiers and auto-select by history length per series: (a) <14 days history → moving average of available days plus a fixed safety multiplier (cold start, see below); (b) 14–~56 days → simple exponential smoothing (SES): L_t = α·y_t + (1−α)·L_{t−1}, forecast = L_t; α≈0.2–0.3 default, or fit by minimizing in-sample SSE via grid search 0.05–0.6. SES handles level with no trend/seasonality and is robust on short noisy series; (c) ≥2 full weekly cycles (~14+ days, ideally 8+ weeks) → Holt-Winters additive with weekly seasonality (period m=7): Level L_t=α(y_t−S_{t−m})+(1−α)(L_{t−1}+T_{t−1}); Trend T_t=β(L_t−L_{t−1})+(1−β)T_{t−1}; Season S_t=γ(y_t−L_t)+(1−γ)S_{t−m}; Forecast ŷ_{t+h}=L_t+h·T_t+S_{t−m+((h−1) mod m)+1}. Use ADDITIVE (not multiplicative) seasonality — blood demand has additive weekday effects and additive avoids divide-by-zero on low-volume rare groups. Initialize L_0 = mean of first week, S = first-week deviations, T_0 = (mean week2 − mean week1)/7.

recommendations.title: Cold-start: ship clinically-grounded defaults so day-one is usable without history
recommendations.detail: On install, seed forecasts from population priors, not zeros. Defaults: (1) ABO/Rh distribution constants to apportion total demand into groups when only aggregate volume is known — region-agnostic default Caucasian-ish blend O+ 37%, A+ 36%, B+ 8%, AB+ 3%, O− 7%, A− 6%, B− 1.5%, AB− 0.5% — but EXPOSE these as an editable config table because distributions are highly region/ethnicity-dependent (e.g., much higher B in South Asia, near-zero Rh-neg in East Asia); shipping one country's numbers hard-coded is a defect. (2) Days-of-supply targets as configurable defaults: RBC 5–7 days, platelets 2–3 days (shelf-life constrained), FFP/cryo larger. (3) During cold start, demand proxy = each branch's own historical issue volume if migrating from a prior system (import CSV), else manual admin-entered expected daily usage per group×component. (4) Blend prior with observed data using a weight that decays as real history accrues (e.g., weight_on_prior = max(0, (N_min − n_days)/N_min)). Never present a forecast as confident until ≥14 days of real data; flag it as 'provisional'.

recommendations.title: Compute the procurement-relevant KPIs with explicit, defensible formulas
recommendations.detail: Wastage/Expiry rate = units discarded (any reason) / units that left available stock, AND a sub-metric expiry-specific wastage = units expired-on-shelf / units available; WHO/AABB benchmark target typically <5% for RBC, with platelets higher due to shelf life. Stock-out rate = (# of group×component×day cells where on-hand=0 OR an urgent request could not be met) / total cells; track separately the more serious 'unmet urgent request' count. Crossmatch-to-Transfusion (C:T) ratio = units crossmatched / units actually transfused; target ≤2.0–2.5 (lower is better; high C:T signals over-ordering and reservation locking that inflates apparent demand and wastage). Transfusion probability/index and MSBOS feed off this. Days-of-supply = current on-hand units / average daily issues (trailing window). Turnaround time (TAT) = time from request received → unit issued (and sub-TATs: request→crossmatch-complete, crossmatch→issue); also collection→available TAT. Donor return rate = repeat donors in period / total donors (and lapsed-donor count for recruitment). Near-expiry inventory = units with ≤X days to expiry (X configurable per component, e.g., RBC 7d, PLT 2d) — drives FEFO issuing and inter-branch transfer triggers. Report each KPI per branch and rolled-up, with trend sparkline and target/threshold coloring.

recommendations.title: Run forecasting and heavy aggregation as scheduled jobs, not per-request
recommendations.detail: Nightly cron job: (1) materialize a daily fact table (see data model) by aggregating the event log; (2) recompute each series' forecast and write to a forecast table with model_used, params (α,β,γ), as_of_date, horizon, point, and safety_quantile; (3) recompute KPI snapshots into a kpi_daily table. Dashboards then read pre-aggregated tables → sub-second loads and reproducible numbers. Do NOT compute Holt-Winters in PHP on page load. Per-request AJAX should only read cached aggregates and do trivial filtering. This also gives you a clean as-of audit trail (forecast made on date D used params P) which matters for 21 CFR Part 11 reproducibility if a clinical decision is ever questioned.

recommendations.title: Be honest about where ML does and does not belong
recommendations.detail: ARIMA/SARIMA, Prophet, gradient boosting, and LSTM are NOT justified for a per-hospital deployment: data volume (often <100 units/day total, far fewer per rare group) is too small for stable training; they need a Python/R runtime (not in the PHP stack); they require model validation/versioning that triggers documentation and Part-11 change-control overhead; and they are hard to explain to a clinical auditor. Holt-Winters with a safety quantile captures ~all realistic signal (weekly seasonality + slow trend) at this scale. Reserve ML only for a future multi-tenant central service that pools data across many hospitals and adds exogenous regressors (surgery schedules, local trauma/holiday calendars) — and even then deliver it as a separate microservice, not inside the PHP monolith. Say plainly: shipping ML now would be cost without payback and adds regulatory surface area.

recommendations.title: Track forecast accuracy and surface it (MAPE/MASE), or the forecast is unaccountable
recommendations.detail: Store actuals next to forecasts and compute rolling accuracy per series: MAE, and MASE (mean absolute scaled error, scaled by naive seasonal forecast — robust to low/zero-volume series where MAPE divides by zero). Show buyers a 'forecast skill' panel proving the model beats naive. Auto-fallback: if Holt-Winters MASE >1 (worse than naive) for a series over the last N days, revert that series to SES or moving average. This guards against Holt-Winters overfitting noise on thin rare-group data.

recommendations.title: Drive operational actions from analytics, don't just display them
recommendations.detail: Close the loop: near-expiry + low-demand-forecast at branch A combined with stock-out-risk forecast at branch B should auto-suggest an inter-branch transfer (ties into existing transfer module). Forecast safety_quantile vs on-hand should set the reorder/collection target and feed the existing alerts module (e.g., 'O-neg projected below 2 days supply in 3 days'). C:T ratio above threshold per ordering physician/ward should raise a stewardship flag. This converts the dashboard from a report into a selling feature.

recommendations.title: Make all targets, benchmarks, and distributions configurable per tenant
recommendations.detail: Because the product is region-agnostic: ABO/Rh population distribution, days-of-supply targets, near-expiry windows per component, KPI thresholds (wastage %, C:T target, stock-out tolerance), seasonality period, and forecast safety quantile must all live in editable config tables, defaulted from cited best-practice but never hard-coded. Buyers in different regions will reject numbers that don't match their epidemiology.

data_model_changes: unit_event_log (event spine — likely the single biggest addition): unit_id FK, event_type ENUM(collected, tested_pass, tested_fail, labeled_available, reserved, crossmatched, issued, transfused, returned_to_stock, discarded, expired, transferred_out, transferred_in, quarantined), event_ts (UTC, precise), actor_user_id, branch_id, related_request_id NULL, reason_code_id NULL, free_text NULL. Append-only, immutable (no UPDATE/DELETE) for 21 CFR Part 11. ALL KPIs and forecasts derive from this — current blood_units status fields are insufficient because they store only current state, not transition timestamps.

reason_codes lookup: code, category (discard_reason, wastage_reason, return_reason, transfer_reason), description. Required to compute WHY units are wasted (expired vs hemolyzed vs broken cold-chain vs over-ordered) — buyers want wastage broken down by cause.

blood_requests must capture timestamps for the TAT chain: requested_ts, crossmatch_started_ts, crossmatch_completed_ts, issued_ts, urgency ENUM(routine, urgent, emergency/MTP), requesting_ward_id, requesting_physician_id, plus outcome (fulfilled, partial, unmet, cancelled) and units_requested vs units_crossmatched vs units_transfused — needed for C:T ratio, stock-out (unmet urgent), and TAT.

crossmatch_records (or fields on request): units_crossmatched count and link to transfusion outcome, so C:T = SUM(crossmatched)/SUM(transfused) is computable; without explicit crossmatched-but-not-transfused tracking, C:T cannot be measured.

demand_fact_daily (materialized nightly): date, branch_id, blood_group, component, units_issued, units_transfused, units_crossmatched, units_requested, units_unmet, units_expired, units_discarded, on_hand_eod. Pre-aggregated source for forecasting and dashboards.

forecast (output table): series_key (branch+group+component), as_of_date, horizon_day, forecast_date, point_qty, safety_quantile_qty, model_used ENUM(moving_avg, ses, holt_winters), params_json (α,β,γ, window), provisional_flag. Append/version by as_of_date for reproducibility.
forecast_accuracy: series_key, eval_date, actual_qty, forecasted_qty, abs_error, mase — for the skill panel and auto-fallback.

kpi_daily (snapshot): date, branch_id, group, component, plus computed KPI columns (wastage_rate, expiry_rate, stockout_rate, ct_ratio, days_of_supply, mean_tat_minutes, near_expiry_count). Pre-computed so dashboards never run heavy queries live.

config_targets per tenant/branch: abo_rh_distribution, days_of_supply_target by component, near_expiry_window_days by component, wastage_threshold, ct_target, stockout_tolerance, safety_quantile, seasonality_period. Editable.

donor table needs first_donation_date and a way to count donations-in-period to compute donor return/retention rate; donations already exist but ensure each links donor_id + donation_ts so repeat vs new is derivable.
risks_and_tradeoffs: PHP has no native, tested time-series/statistics library: Holt-Winters, parameter fitting (grid search), quantile estimation, MASE must be hand-implemented and unit-tested. Risk of subtle bugs (e.g., seasonal index drift, divide-by-zero on zero-volume rare groups) that silently corrupt forecasts. Mitigate with a fixed test fixture of known input→output series.

True scheduling is a stack gap: reliable nightly jobs need OS cron / Windows Task Scheduler or a daemon. The 'offline-sync queue / request-triggered cron emulation' pattern common in pure-PHP shops produces non-deterministic run times and missed nights, breaking reproducibility — unacceptable for a clinical KPI/forecast that may be cited. State plainly: a real scheduler is required, not pseudo-cron.

Thin-data instability: rare groups (AB−, O−) and platelets at small branches may have many zero-demand days. Holt-Winters and MAPE behave badly here; additive HW + MASE + auto-fallback to SES/moving-average is mandatory, not optional.

Garbage-in: every KPI and forecast is only as good as the event log. If staff don't record transfused/returned/discarded events with timestamps and reason codes, C:T, wastage-by-cause, and TAT are all wrong. This is a workflow/UX and training risk, not just schema — capture must be low-friction (e.g., barcode scan at each transition) or data quality collapses.

Forecasts driving auto-orders create liability: if the system recommends collection/reorder targets and a stock-out causes a clinical event, the buyer will scrutinize the model. Keep humans in the loop (suggest, not auto-execute), log as-of params, and label provisional forecasts — this is both a safety and a Part-11 reproducibility requirement.

Region-agnostic distributions: hard-coding any single population's ABO/Rh split or benchmark target will produce wrong group-level forecasts and KPI red/green flags in other regions; must be config-driven, which adds onboarding complexity.

C:T ratio is only meaningful if crossmatched-but-not-transfused units are explicitly tracked and returned to stock; partial implementations that only log transfusions will report a misleadingly perfect C:T and miss the wastage signal the metric exists to catch.
php_mysql_feasibility: Adequate with two clear caveats. KPI COMPUTATION: fully feasible in MySQL — wastage rate, stock-out rate, C:T ratio, days-of-supply, TAT, donor return rate, and near-expiry counts are all GROUP BY / window-function aggregations over the unit_event_log and blood_requests tables. Use MySQL 8.0+ window functions (LAG, SUM OVER, COUNT OVER) for rolling windows and EOD on-hand; pre-materialize into kpi_daily via a nightly job so dashboards read cheap. FORECASTING: moving average and SES are trivial in SQL/PHP. Holt-Winters is feasible in PHP but must be hand-coded (no library), run as a batch job over demand_fact_daily, and unit-tested against known fixtures — this is the main engineering cost. WHAT BREAKS / WHAT IS NEEDED: (1) A REAL scheduler (OS cron / Task Scheduler / daemon) is required for deterministic nightly aggregation and forecasting; request-triggered pseudo-cron is insufficient for a sellable, auditable system — state this plainly to the buyer. (2) PHP's lack of a stats library means quantiles, parameter fitting, and accuracy metrics (MASE) are bespoke code needing test coverage. (3) Anything beyond Holt-Winters (ARIMA, ML) is NOT feasible in-stack and should not be attempted in the PHP monolith; defer to a future separate Python service only if multi-tenant data pooling ever justifies it. (4) The append-only immutable event log needed for both analytics and 21 CFR Part 11 must be enforced at the DB/app layer (no UPDATE/DELETE; corrections via compensating events) — MySQL supports this via triggers/permissions but it must be deliberately designed, not assumed.

executive_summary: A sellable multi-branch blood bank system handles special-category health data (donors + recipients) and GxP-regulated release decisions, so it must clear the strictest common denominator across GDPR (privacy), 21 CFR Part 11 (electronic records/signatures), AABB Standards + EU GMP Annex 11 (computerized systems), and ISO 27001/HIPAA-grade controls. This requires: (a) fine-grained permission-based RBAC with enforced segregation of duties so the person who performs/interprets testing cannot also release the unit, plus audited break-glass; (b) modern credential security — Argon2id/bcrypt hashing, mandatory MFA for release/admin roles, idle + absolute session timeouts, and lockout with throttling; (c) TLS 1.2+ in transit and encryption at rest via MySQL TDE for the tablespace PLUS application-level (envelope) field encryption for direct identifiers, with keys held in a KMS/HSM outside MySQL; (d) GDPR-grade privacy: documented lawful basis (donor consent is withdrawable; recipient processing rests on vital-interest/healthcare provision, NOT consent), data-subject-rights workflows, pseudonymization, and legally-mandated long retention that overrides erasure; (e) Part 11 electronic signatures (two distinct ID components, signature manifestation captured in the record, cryptographically bound to an append-only audit trail). Vanilla PHP/MySQL can implement most of this but CANNOT by itself provide tamper-evident immutability, real key isolation, or trustworthy time — those must be added with hash-chaining, a KMS, and an authoritative time source. Plainly: the stack is viable only if augmented; an unaugmented LAMP build will fail a Part 11 / Annex 11 audit and a GDPR DPIA.

recommendations.title: Permission-based RBAC, not role strings
recommendations.detail: Replace any single role VARCHAR with a normalized model: users — roles (m:n via user_roles) — role_permissions — permissions, where permissions are fine-grained verbs on objects (e.g. donation.screen, test.perform, test.interpret, unit.label, unit.quarantine_release, unit.issue, request.approve, transfer.authorize, donor.read_pii, audit.read, user.manage, config.compatibility_rules.edit). Enforce server-side on EVERY endpoint via a central authorize($permission, $context) gate — never rely on hiding UI. Scope every permission to a branch_id so a tech at branch A cannot act on branch B; multi-branch users get explicit grants. Cache permissions per session but re-check on each mutating call.

recommendations.title: Enforced Segregation of Duties (SoD) for unit release
recommendations.detail: Model SoD as data, not policy docs. The donation→release pipeline must require distinct user IDs at each gate: collector ≠ tester; for critical infectious-marker results require a second independent verification (test.perform vs test.interpret held by different people); the person who performed/interpreted screening MUST NOT hold unit.quarantine_release for that same unit. Enforce with a server-side check: on release, reject if released_by IN (collected_by, tested_by, interpreted_by) for that unit. Maintain a static SoD conflict matrix table (conflicting_permission_pairs) and block role assignments that violate it. AABB Standards require a qualified second review before product release; 21 CFR 606.100/630 require independent verification of donor suitability and test results.

recommendations.title: Break-glass emergency access with mandatory logging
recommendations.detail: Provide a break_glass workflow: an authorized user can elevate to read otherwise-restricted PII or release in a life-threatening emergency by entering a reason code + free-text justification; the system grants a TIME-BOXED elevated session (e.g. 30 min), writes a high-severity immutable audit event BEFORE granting, raises a real-time alert to a supervisor/DPO, and flags the session for mandatory post-hoc review. Break-glass must never bypass logging or signature capture — it bypasses only the pre-authorization, not accountability. Required to satisfy emergency-issue clinical reality without weakening the default least-privilege posture.

recommendations.title: Password hashing: Argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt
recommendations.detail: Use PHP password_hash() with PASSWORD_ARGON2ID (memory_cost >= 19 MiB, time_cost >= 2, parallelism 1 per OWASP) or PASSWORD_BCRYPT cost >= 12 as fallback. Never MD5/SHA without salt. Store only the hash; use password_verify() and password_needs_rehash() to upgrade transparently. Enforce a password policy (length >= 12, breach-list check) and rotation only on suspected compromise (NIST 800-63B discourages forced periodic rotation).

recommendations.title: Multi-factor authentication
recommendations.detail: Mandate MFA (TOTP RFC 6238 via authenticator app, or WebAuthn/FIDO2 for phishing resistance) for all privileged roles: release, admin, DPO, config editors, and any break-glass elevation. TOTP is implementable in pure PHP (e.g. HOTP/TOTP libs) with secrets stored field-encrypted. WebAuthn is preferable for the sellable bar but needs the browser API + a relying-party verification step in PHP. Provide recovery codes (hashed). 21 CFR 11.10(d)/11.300 and GDPR Art 32 expect strong authentication for sensitive-data access.

recommendations.title: Session management: idle + absolute timeout, secure cookies
recommendations.detail: Idle timeout 15 min for clinical/release roles; absolute session lifetime cap (e.g. 8–12 h) regardless of activity. Regenerate session ID on login and on privilege change (prevent fixation). Cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, short-lived. Store sessions server-side (DB or Redis), not in client. Bind session to a re-authentication step before signing (Part 11 11.200 requires the signing component be re-entered for non-continuous sessions).

recommendations.title: Account lockout and brute-force throttling
recommendations.detail: Progressive throttling + temporary lockout after N failed attempts (e.g. 5), with exponential backoff and per-account + per-IP rate limiting; log all failures to the audit trail; alert on repeated lockouts. Protect MFA endpoints equally. Avoid permanent lockout (DoS risk) — use time-boxed locks plus admin unlock. 21 CFR 11.300(d) requires detecting and reporting unauthorized attempts.

recommendations.title: Encryption in transit
recommendations.detail: TLS 1.2+ (prefer 1.3) for all browser-server and server-server (inter-branch sync) traffic; HSTS; disable legacy ciphers. Enable TLS on the MySQL client connection (REQUIRE SSL on DB accounts) so app-DB traffic is encrypted, especially for multi-branch/remote DB topologies. mTLS for the inter-branch sync channel.

recommendations.title: Encryption at rest: TDE + application-level field encryption
recommendations.detail: Two layers. (1) MySQL TDE (InnoDB tablespace encryption, available in MySQL 8 Enterprise and MariaDB; AES) protects whole files at rest against disk/backup theft but does NOT protect against an attacker with DB query access. (2) Application-level (envelope) encryption of direct identifiers and the most sensitive fields (donor/recipient name, national ID, contact, infectious-disease results) using AES-256-GCM via PHP openssl/libsodium, with a per-record data key wrapped by a master key in a KMS. This keeps plaintext out of SELECT results, logs, and replicas. Trade-off: encrypted fields cannot be indexed/searched directly — use blind indexes (HMAC of normalized value) for exact-match lookup, accept loss of range/LIKE queries.

recommendations.title: Key management outside MySQL
recommendations.detail: Do NOT store encryption keys in PHP source, config files in webroot, or the same DB. Use a KMS/HSM (e.g. HashiCorp Vault, cloud KMS, or PKCS#11 HSM) or at minimum an OS keyring with envelope encryption: KMS holds the master key, app fetches/wraps data keys at runtime, keys are rotatable without re-encrypting all data (re-wrap data keys only). MySQL TDE keyring must also use a real keyring plugin, not file-based keyring on the same host for the sellable bar. Document key rotation, escrow, and access in a key-management SOP (ISO 27001 A.10 / Annex 11).

recommendations.title: GDPR lawful basis & consent capture (distinguish donor vs recipient)
recommendations.detail: Capture and version the lawful basis per processing purpose. DONOR: explicit consent for donation + health screening (Art 9(2)(a)), withdrawable — but withdrawal cannot delete safety/traceability records mandated by law. RECIPIENT/PATIENT: do NOT rely on consent; rely on Art 9(2)(h) (provision of health care) and/or 9(2)(c) (vital interests) — patients in transfusion emergencies cannot consent. Store consent_records (subject_id, purpose, basis, version, timestamp, captured_by, withdrawal_ts) immutably. Surface a privacy notice and record its version shown.

recommendations.title: Data-subject rights workflows
recommendations.detail: Implement endpoints/processes for access (Art 15 export of a subject's data), rectification (Art 16, as a corrective versioned record never a destructive overwrite of GxP data), erasure (Art 17 — MUST be refusable where retention is legally required for blood safety/traceability; implement as restriction/blocking + crypto-shredding of non-mandatory PII instead of deletion), restriction (Art 18), and portability (Art 20, machine-readable export). Every DSR action is itself an audited event. Provide a DPO dashboard.

recommendations.title: Retention periods (research-backed, long and legally binding)
recommendations.detail: Blood records have statutory minimums that OVERRIDE erasure requests. EU Directive 2002/98/EC + Commission Directive 2005/61/EC require traceability data linking donor↔donation↔component↔recipient be kept at least 30 YEARS. US FDA 21 CFR 606.160(d) requires blood establishment records be kept at least 10 years (with some records — e.g. donor deferral/look-back — kept indefinitely/for the longer of 10 years or until product disposition + further). AABB aligns with these. Implement a retention_policy table keyed by record_class with min_retention_years and a legal_hold flag; the purge job must NEVER delete records under retention or legal hold. Default to the strictest applicable (30y for traceability) so it ports across regions.

recommendations.title: Pseudonymization & data minimization
recommendations.detail: Separate direct identifiers into a restricted identity table referenced by a surrogate subject key; operational/analytical tables and reports use the pseudonym, not name/ID. Re-identification requires a separately-permissioned join (donor.read_pii). Pseudonymize data sent to non-clinical reporting/analytics and to lower environments (never copy production PII to dev/test — use synthetic or masked data). Satisfies GDPR Art 25 (data protection by design) and Art 32.

recommendations.title: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signatures
recommendations.detail: Each signing event must: use a signature composed of two distinct components — typically user ID (already authenticated) + a private password/PIN re-entered at signing (11.200(a)(1)); for a continuous session the first signing uses both components and subsequent ones at least one, with session controls (11.200(a)(1)(i-ii)). The signed record must DISPLAY the signature manifestation (11.50): printed/displayed name of signer, date & time of signing (from an authoritative/trusted clock, not client-supplied), and the MEANING of the signature (e.g. 'reviewed', 'approved for release', 'verified result'). Signatures must be linked to their records so they cannot be cut/copied/transferred (11.70). Signatures are equivalent to handwritten (11.3). Maintain the certification to FDA that e-signatures are legally binding (11.100(c)) as an organizational artifact.

recommendations.title: Immutable, tamper-evident audit trail bound to signatures
recommendations.detail: Audit trail must be computer-generated, time-stamped, capture old+new values, who/when/why, and be non-modifiable by users (11.10(e), Annex 11 §9). Make it tamper-EVIDENT in MySQL via hash-chaining: each audit row stores hash = H(prev_hash || row_payload), creating a blockchain-style chain that detects insertion/deletion/edit. Periodically sign/anchor the chain head (e.g. nightly digest signed by a server key or sent to a WORM store / external timestamping authority RFC 3161). Electronic signatures store the audit_event hash they sign over, binding signature→record→chain. Use append-only DB privileges (app account has INSERT only on audit_log, no UPDATE/DELETE) and DB triggers that reject UPDATE/DELETE.

recommendations.title: Trusted time source
recommendations.detail: Client clocks are untrustworthy for Part 11/Annex 11. Derive all signing and audit timestamps server-side from an NTP-synced server clock; for the highest bar, RFC 3161 timestamp tokens from a TSA for signature events. Record timezone in UTC. This is an explicit gap the PHP app must close — never accept a browser-supplied timestamp for a signed/audited action.

recommendations.title: DPIA, breach notification, and SOPs as deliverables
recommendations.detail: Ship the system with a Data Protection Impact Assessment template (Art 35, mandatory for large-scale special-category processing), a 72-hour breach-notification procedure (Art 33/34), validation/IQ-OQ-PQ documentation (Annex 11 §4, computerized system validation), and SOPs for access control, key management, backup/restore, and audit review. A sellable GxP system is the software PLUS this documentation; hospitals' auditors will ask for it.

recommendations.title: Secure inter-branch sync & offline queue
recommendations.detail: The offline-sync queue and inter-branch transfer carry PII and must be encrypted at rest in the queue (field-level), transmitted over mTLS, signed for integrity, and idempotent with conflict resolution that never silently overwrites a signed release. Queued audit/signature events must preserve original server-trusted timestamps and re-chain correctly on the central node. Reconcile SoD across branches (a release signed offline must still satisfy distinct-signer rules on merge).

risks_and_tradeoffs: Field-level encryption defeats SQL indexing/search: name and national ID become non-searchable except via blind indexes (exact-match only); range queries, LIKE, and sorting on encrypted PII are lost — design lookups around surrogate keys and blind indexes early.

MySQL hash-chained audit gives tamper-EVIDENCE, not tamper-PREVENTION. A DBA/root with full DB+host access can recompute the whole chain. True immutability requires external anchoring (WORM storage, RFC 3161 TSA, or write to a separate append-only system) — pure MySQL cannot guarantee it alone.

MySQL TDE protects only files at rest; anyone with query access still sees plaintext. It is necessary but insufficient — hence the app-level layer. Community MySQL TDE/keyring options are weaker than Enterprise; file-based keyring on the same host provides little real protection.

Key management is the hardest part on a LAMP stack: doing it without a real KMS/HSM (keys in config/env) is a common but audit-failing shortcut. Selling into hospitals likely requires shipping or integrating a KMS, adding deployment complexity beyond vanilla PHP.

GDPR erasure vs statutory retention will conflict: erasure requests for donors/recipients MUST often be refused for 10–30 years for blood-safety traceability. This must be documented and defensible, or the vendor risks GDPR complaints; implement as restriction/crypto-shred of non-mandatory fields, not deletion.
Trusted time and trusted random/crypto are environmental dependencies (NTP, libsodium, OpenSSL, possibly TSA) that the deploying hospital's infra must provide; the app cannot self-certify time.

Offline-sync + SoD interact badly: an offline release may pass local SoD but conflict on merge; without careful conflict resolution you can produce a unit released by a single identity across nodes, violating SoD.

21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 compliance is also organizational (validation IQ/OQ/PQ, SOPs, signed certifications) — software alone cannot make a customer compliant; the sellable bar includes documentation deliverables, not just code.

Plain PHP session handling and CSRF/XSS hardening must be rigorous (output encoding, prepared statements, CSRF tokens, CSP) — a single injection flaw exposes all decrypted PII at the app tier where keys live, the highest-value target.
php_mysql_feasibility: Vanilla PHP/MySQL/AJAX can implement the MAJORITY of this bar and is a defensible foundation, but NOT unaugmented. What PHP/MySQL does well natively: Argon2id/bcrypt via password_hash(); AES-256-GCM field encryption via libsodium/openssl; TOTP MFA; server-side sessions with idle/absolute timeouts and lockout; permission-based RBAC and SoD enforced in application logic + relational tables; TLS via the web server and REQUIRE SSL DB accounts; hash-chained audit rows and INSERT-only DB grants with UPDATE/DELETE-blocking triggers; Part 11 signature components (re-enter password at signing) and manifestation rows. What the stack CANNOT do at the sellable bar and MUST add: (1) Real key isolation — keys cannot live in PHP config/DB; requires an external KMS/HSM (Vault, cloud KMS, or PKCS#11). (2) True immutability/non-repudiation of the audit trail — MySQL alone is tamper-evident at best; needs external anchoring (RFC 3161 TSA, WORM/append-only store, or signed nightly digests off-host) because root/DBA can rewrite a self-contained chain. (3) Trusted time — must come from NTP/TSA, not the app or client. (4) MySQL TDE for files at rest requires MySQL 8 Enterprise or MariaDB with a proper keyring plugin (a licensing/edition cost), not the default community file engine. (5) WebAuthn/FIDO2 (phishing-resistant MFA, the stronger bar) needs added relying-party verification code. (6) Searchable encryption is unsolved natively — blind indexes give exact match only. (7) The compliance posture also demands non-software deliverables (DPIA, CSV validation IQ/OQ/PQ, SOPs, Part 11 §11.100(c) certification) that ship WITH the product. Verdict: feasible as PHP/MySQL core + mandatory bolt-ons (KMS, external audit anchoring/WORM, trusted time, possibly MySQL Enterprise/MariaDB for TDE). An unaugmented LAMP build will fail a Part 11/Annex 11 audit and a GDPR Art 35 DPIA — say so to the buyer rather than designing to a happy path.
